schema.text: Open-label randomized phase II trial (GLIAA, NOA-10/ARO 2013-1, NCT01252459) comparing FET-PET-based versus T1 gadolinium MRI-based target delineation for re-irradiation of recurrent glioblastoma. The primary endpoint is progression-free survival from randomization.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Minimization by time since the end of first radiotherapy (14 months or less versus more than 14 months), prior temozolomide (7 cycles or fewer versus more than 7), maximum MRI tumor diameter (3 cm or less versus more than 3 cm), and MGMT status (methylated, unmethylated, or not yet determined).

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Allocation is 1:1. Both arms receive the same dose. Only the GTV definition differs.

arms.label: Arm A, FET-PET
arms.text: GTV starts from FET uptake greater than 1.8 plus or minus 0.1 times normal brain, then visually verified by nuclear medicine and the radiation oncologist. Re-irradiation is 39 Gy in 13 fractions of 3 Gy, five days a week, to the PTV, with the 95% isodose surrounding the PTV.

arms.label: Arm B, MRI
arms.text: GTV is tumor-related contrast enhancement on T1 gadolinium MRI, with no safety margin, agreed with a neuroradiologist. The same 39 Gy in 13 fractions of 3 Gy is delivered.

NCT01252459.schema_source: Open-access protocol, Oehlke et al., BMC Cancer 2016 (PMID 27716184). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Age at least 18, Karnofsky performance status above 60%, recurrent glioblastoma not eligible for resection or with macroscopic residual tumor after resection of the recurrence, and histologic glioblastoma at initial or repeat diagnosis.
Prior radiotherapy for high-grade glioma to 59.4 to 60 Gy at 1.8 to 2.0 Gy per fraction, with at least 6 months between the end of that course and randomization.
Recurrent tumor visible on both FET-PET and T1 gadolinium MRI, with maximum diameter, or the sum of diameters if multifocal, of 1 to 6 cm on each modality.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: This ancillary molecular analysis restates GOG-0249 (NCT00807768), which randomized early-stage endometrial cancer to vaginal cuff brachytherapy plus chemotherapy or pelvic radiotherapy. The brachytherapy dose in gray is not printed in this paper.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Stratified before randomization by intent to use vaginal cuff brachytherapy in the pelvic radiotherapy arm, and by lymphadenectomy versus no lymphadenectomy.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients were allocated 1:1. Three hundred one were assigned to pelvic radiotherapy and 300 to vaginal cuff brachytherapy plus chemotherapy.

arms.label: Vaginal cuff brachytherapy plus chemotherapy
arms.text: Vaginal cuff brachytherapy followed by three cycles of paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 over 3 hours plus carboplatin AUC 6 every 21 days.

arms.label: Pelvic radiotherapy
arms.text: Pelvic radiotherapy, 45 to 50.4 Gy over 5 weeks.

NCT00807768.schema_source: Trial report, Kuroki et al., Gynecologic Oncology 2026 (PMID 42190623). Read from the full text.
eligibility: FIGO 2009 stage I endometrioid carcinoma meeting GOG protocol 33 high-intermediate-risk criteria, and the stage I to II population described for this trial. Retrospective central pathology review confirmed eligibility. The full high-intermediate-risk definition is cited rather than reprinted.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Randomized multicenter phase III trial (GOG-0258, NCT00942357) comparing chemoradiotherapy followed by chemotherapy with chemotherapy alone after surgery for stage III or IVA endometrial carcinoma. The primary endpoint is relapse-free survival.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Randomization was stratified by age and by the presence or absence of gross residual disease.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: The two regimens were assigned 1:1 in permuted blocks.

arms.label: Chemoradiotherapy
arms.text: Cisplatin 50 mg/m2 intravenously on days 1 and 29 with volume-directed external-beam radiotherapy, then carboplatin AUC 5 to 6 plus paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 every 21 days for four cycles, with G-CSF. Pelvic radiotherapy, with or without para-aortic fields, was planned as 45 Gy in 25 fractions of 1.8 Gy. Intensity-modulated radiotherapy and vaginal brachytherapy were allowed only in this group.

arms.label: Chemotherapy alone
arms.text: Carboplatin AUC 6 plus paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 every 21 days for six cycles.

NCT00942357.schema_source: Trial report, Matei et al., The New England Journal of Medicine 2019 (PMID 31189035). Read from the full text.
eligibility: The report analyzes surgically treated stage III or IVA endometrial carcinoma. Detailed eligibility beyond stage, central pathology review, and gross residual disease as a stratification factor is in the protocol and is not fully restated in the printed methods.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Open-label randomized phase III trial (NRG Oncology/GOG-0263/KGOG 1008, NCT01101451) of adjuvant radiotherapy versus weekly cisplatin chemoradiotherapy after radical hysterectomy for intermediate-risk early-stage cervical cancer. The primary endpoint is recurrence-free survival.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Dynamic allocation by capillary lymphatic space involvement (positive versus negative), depth of stromal invasion (deep versus middle versus superficial), performance status (0 or 1 versus 2), planned modality (IMRT versus 3D conformal radiotherapy), and cooperative group.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients were assigned with equal probability between 3 and 8 weeks after surgery. External-beam radiotherapy was given without brachytherapy.

arms.label: Radiotherapy
arms.text: Pelvic external-beam radiotherapy, prescribed as 50.4 Gy in 28 fractions, five fractions a week, with daily fractions of 1.8 to 2.0 Gy over 4.5 to 5.5 weeks. A four-field megavoltage technique was used. Cobalt-60 was allowed if the source-to-skin distance was greater than 80 cm. IMRT required IROC Houston credentialing.

arms.label: Chemoradiotherapy
arms.text: The same radiotherapy plus six weekly cycles of cisplatin 40 mg/m2 during radiotherapy.

NCT01101451.schema_source: Trial report, Ryu et al., Annals of Oncology 2025 (PMID 40947016). Read from the full text.
eligibility: FIGO 2009 stage IB to IIA cervical cancer with intermediate-risk factors after radical hysterectomy and pelvic lymphadenectomy.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Patients with locoregionally advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma were randomized 1:1 at six centres.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Sequential chemoradiotherapy was compared with induction chemotherapy plus concurrent chemoradiotherapy. Both induction regimens used gemcitabine and cisplatin.

arms.label: Sequential chemoradiotherapy
arms.text: Two cycles of gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 on days 1 and 8 plus cisplatin 25 mg/m2 on days 1 to 3 every 3 weeks, then radiotherapy alone, then two further cycles of the same chemotherapy.

arms.label: Induction plus concurrent chemoradiotherapy
arms.text: Two cycles of the same induction chemotherapy, then radiotherapy concurrent with weekly cisplatin 30 mg/m2.

schema.note: 420 patients were randomized (210 per group). The radiotherapy dose is not stated in this abstract.

NCT03366415.schema_source: The nasopharyngeal sequential-versus-concurrent abstract (PMID 40705321) states both chemotherapy-radiotherapy sequences and the drug doses.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: CLINICAL INVESTIGATION Stereotactic Body Proton Therapy Versus Conventionally Fractionated Proton Therapy for Early Prostate Cancer: A Randomized, Controlled, Phase 3 Trial Diego A.S.

arms.label: Assignment
arms.text: Eligible participants were randomly assigned initially at a 1:1 ratio and later at a 2:1 ratio to SBPT (38 Gy in 5 fractions) or CFPT (79.2 Gy in 44 fractions).

NCT01230866.schema_source: Toesca et al., International journal of radiation oncology, biology, physics 2024 (PMID 38972465). The full text was read.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Clinical Investigation Comparison of 36 Gy, 20 Gy, or No Radiation Therapy After 6 Cycles of EBVP Chemotherapy and Complete Remission in Early-Stage Hodgkin Lymphoma Without Risk Factors: Results of the EORT-GELA H9-F Intergroup Randomized Trial Jose´ Thomas, MD, * Christophe Ferme´, MD, y Evert M.

schema.label: Radiotherapy
schema.text: Patients in complete remission after chemotherapy were randomized to no RT, low-dose RT (20 Gy in 10 fractions), or standard-dose involvedfield RT (36 Gy in 18 fractions).

NCT00005584.schema_source: Thomas et al., International journal of radiation oncology, biology, physics 2018 (PMID 29229324). The full text was read.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: This quality-of-life analysis restates the randomized phase III comparison of prophylactic cranial irradiation with or without hippocampal avoidance (NCT01780675) in small-cell lung cancer. In this report, 168 patients were randomized.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Both arms used the same prescription. The paper does not restate the allocation ratio.

arms.label: PCI
arms.text: 25 Gy in 10 fractions, five fractions a week.

arms.label: HA-PCI
arms.text: The same 25 Gy in 10 fractions. The mean dose to the hippocampal avoidance zone was limited to 8.5 Gy.

NCT01780675.schema_source: Open-access trial report, Albers et al., JTO Clinical and Research Reports 2023 (PMID 37284297). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Patients first received four courses of platinum-etoposide alone for stage IV disease, or concurrent chemoradiotherapy for stages I to III, and then PCI. At least 3 weeks separated the last chemotherapy from the start of PCI.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Randomized phase III trial HD16 (NCT00736320) of PET-guided treatment in early-stage favorable Hodgkin lymphoma. The primary endpoint is progression-free survival from completion of staging.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Central 1:1 randomization before treatment, stratified by site, age (under 45 versus 45 or older), sex, B symptoms, disease above versus below the diaphragm, albumin (below 40 g/L versus at least 40 g/L), and initial bulk of at least 5 cm.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Both groups received two cycles of ABVD and a centrally reviewed PET/CT (PET-2).

arms.label: Combined modality
arms.text: Two cycles of ABVD followed by 20 Gy involved-field radiotherapy for every patient, regardless of the PET-2 result.

arms.label: PET-guided
arms.text: Two cycles of ABVD, with 20 Gy involved-field radiotherapy only if PET-2 is positive, defined as a Deauville score of 3 or higher.

NCT00736320.schema_source: Trial report, Fuchs et al., Leukemia 2023 (PMID 37845285). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Age 18 to 75 with newly diagnosed classical Hodgkin lymphoma in clinical stage I or II, or nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma in stage IB, IIA, or IIB, and none of the GHSG risk factors: large mediastinal mass (at least one third of the maximum thoracic diameter), extranodal lesions, elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (at least 50 mm/h without B symptoms, or at least 30 mm/h with B symptoms), or three or more involved nodal areas.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: This quality-assurance paper restates the phase III HD17 trial (NCT01356680) for early-stage unfavorable Hodgkin lymphoma. All patients received the same chemotherapy. Radiotherapy then differed by arm.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: The standard arm gave involved-field radiotherapy to every patient. The experimental arm limited radiotherapy to patients with a positive PET after chemotherapy.

arms.label: Standard
arms.text: Two cycles of escalated BEACOPP and two cycles of ABVD, then 30 Gy involved-field radiotherapy.

arms.label: PET-guided
arms.text: The same chemotherapy. Patients with a PET-positive result after chemotherapy received 30 Gy involved-node radiotherapy. The Deauville cutoff used to call PET positive is not printed in this paper.

NCT01356680.schema_source: Open-access trial report, Oertel et al., Advances in Radiation Oncology 2022 (PMID 36896214). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Age 18 to 60 with early-stage unfavorable Hodgkin lymphoma: Ann Arbor stage I or IIA with any of the GHSG risk factors named for this program (mediastinal bulk, extranodal involvement, elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate, or three or more nodal areas), or stage IIB with an elevated sedimentation rate and/or at least three nodal areas.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Multicenter nonblinded randomized trial (HD.6, NCT00002561) of ABVD alone versus treatment that includes subtotal nodal irradiation for previously untreated stage IA or IIA nonbulky Hodgkin lymphoma. The primary endpoint is 12-year overall survival. The risk-profile definition that separates favorable from unfavorable disease is not restated in this report.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients were randomly assigned to ABVD alone or to a radiation-based strategy. Allocation was concealed.

arms.label: ABVD alone
arms.text: Both favorable-risk and unfavorable-risk patients received ABVD. Patients in complete or unconfirmed complete remission after two cycles received four cycles in total. Patients who had not reached that response received six cycles.

arms.label: Radiation-based therapy
arms.text: Favorable-risk patients received subtotal nodal irradiation alone. Unfavorable-risk patients received two cycles of ABVD followed by subtotal nodal irradiation. The target was the mantle field, the spleen, and the para-aortic nodes. A linear accelerator treated parallel opposed fields to a mid-plane dose of 35 Gy in 20 daily fractions.

NCT00002561.schema_source: Trial report, Meyer et al., The New England Journal of Medicine 2011 (PMID 22149921). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Previously untreated stage IA or IIA nonbulky Hodgkin lymphoma. Eligibility details beyond that stage definition are referred to an earlier publication and the supplement and are not restated here.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Adults with hepatocellular carcinoma or liver metastases refractory to standard treatment, ECOG 0 to 3, life expectancy over 3 months, and worst liver pain at least 4 out of 10 that was stable for up to 7 days were eligible.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Minimisation was stratified by centre and cancer type (hepatocellular carcinoma versus liver metastases).

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Single-fraction liver radiotherapy plus best supportive care was compared with best supportive care alone.

arms.label: Radiotherapy plus best supportive care
arms.text: 8 Gy in one fraction to the liver, with ondansetron 8 mg or equivalent and dexamethasone 4 mg orally 1 to 2 hours before radiotherapy, plus best supportive care.

arms.label: Best supportive care
arms.text: Best supportive care alone, including non-opioid or opioid analgesia, dexamethasone, or both.

schema.note: 66 patients were screened and assigned (33 per group).

NCT02511522.schema_source: The CCTG HE1 abstract (PMID 39245060) states the 8 Gy liver radiotherapy versus best supportive care randomization and stratification.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: HiLo was a factorial trial of radioactive iodine ablation for well-differentiated thyroid cancer.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients were assigned 1:1:1:1 to iodine dose and preparation method.

arms.label: Low dose, rhTSH
arms.text: 1.1 GBq iodine-131 after recombinant human thyroid-stimulating hormone.

arms.label: Low dose, withdrawal
arms.text: 1.1 GBq iodine-131 after thyroid hormone withdrawal.

arms.label: High dose, rhTSH
arms.text: 3.7 GBq iodine-131 after recombinant human thyroid-stimulating hormone.

arms.label: High dose, withdrawal
arms.text: 3.7 GBq iodine-131 after thyroid hormone withdrawal.

schema.note: 438 patients were randomly assigned.

NCT00415233.schema_source: The HiLo long-term abstract (PMID 30501974) states the four-way randomization of iodine dose and preparation.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Intermediate-risk localized prostate cancer by the D'Amico grouping (not low risk and not high risk: clinical stage, PSA, and biopsy Gleason score).

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: All patients receive 3 months of neoadjuvant androgen deprivation, then iodine-125 transperineal brachytherapy planned to at least 144 Gy to the clinical target volume (prostate plus margin). They are then randomized to adjuvant androgen deprivation or no further androgen deprivation.

arms.label: Adjuvant ADT
arms.text: Nine months of adjuvant androgen deprivation after iodine-125 brachytherapy.

arms.label: No adjuvant ADT
arms.text: Iodine-125 brachytherapy without adjuvant androgen deprivation.

schema.note: Stratification factors are not stated in the protocol paper.

NCT00664456.schema_source: The open-access SHIP 0804 protocol (PMID 20964826) states the randomization after neoadjuvant androgen deprivation and the iodine-125 dose.
eligibility: a. Be 20 to 75 years of age, with a definitive histological diagnosis of PCa by needle biopsy.

Have intermediate-risk PCa according to D'Amico's stratification. Patients with clinical stage T1c or T2a, PSA <= 10 ng/mL and biopsy Gleason score <= 6 are defined as low-risk, and patients with >= T2c, a PSA > 20 ng/mL or a biopsy Gleason score >= 8 are defined as high-risk. The remaining patients are defined as the intermediate-risk group.
c. Be previously untreated.
d. Demonstrate appropriate bone marrow, hepatic and renal function in laboratory tests within two weeks prior to registration.
a) Leukocyte count >= 2,000/μL
b) Hemoglobin level >= 10.0 g/dL
c) Platelet count >= 10.0 x 10^4/μL
Excluded: a. Have previously received surgery for PCa.
Excluded: b. Have PSA > 20 ng/mL.
Excluded: c. Have a biopsy Gleason score >= 8.
Excluded: e. Exhibit clinical stage >= T2c.
The published laboratory inequalities for creatinine, AST, or ALT are printed as lower bounds, so those limits are not restated.

schema.text: Stereotactic radiotherapy for neovascular age-related macular degeneration (STAR): a pivotal, randomised, double-masked, sham-controlled device trial.

arms.label: Assignment
arms.text: Participants were randomly allocated in a 2:1 ratio to 16-Gray (Gy) SRT delivered using a robotically controlled device or sham SRT, stratified by treatment centre.

NCT02243878.schema_source: Jackson et al., Lancet (London, England) 2024 (PMID 38876132). The full text was read.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Background: The multicenter, randomized UPGRADE-RT trial (NCT02442375) evaluated the safety and clinical benefit of elective neck radiotherapy with reduced versus standard dose in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (SCC).

arms.label: Assignment
arms.text: Dose for elective neck irradiation was randomly assigned (ratio 2:1 to dose reduction, 43 Gy versus control, 50 Gy).

schema.text: : Three hundred patients with cT2-4 N0-2 M0 SCC of the oropharynx, larynx or hypopharynx received definitive accelerated radiotherapy alone (34 fractions of 2 Gy in 5.5 weeks).

NCT02442375.schema_source: van et al., Radiotherapy and oncology 2025 (PMID 41057084). The full text was read.

schema.label: Radiotherapy
schema.text: Each institution produced plans for short course (SCRT, 5 /C2 5 Gy) and long course (LCRT, 25 /C2 2 Gy) treatment, using volumetric modulated arc therapy on different dose planning systems.

NCT02945566.schema_source: Appelt et al., Technical innovations & patient support in radiation oncology 2019 (PMID 32095545). The full text was read.

arms.label: Assignment
arms.text: The patients were randomly assigned to either the training group (N = 161) or the test group (N = 68) in a 7:3 ratio.

NCT02979691.schema_source: Zheng et al., Physics and imaging in radiation oncology 2025 (PMID 41333544). The full text was read.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Hepatocellular carcinoma or oligometastatic disease to the liver suitable for stereotactic ablative radiotherapy. This is a single-arm phase II study of kilovoltage intrafraction monitoring, not a randomized dose comparison.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: All treated patients receive liver SABR with kilovoltage intrafraction monitoring. The radiation oncologist chooses a protocol dose according to histology and clinical scenario.

arms.label: Hepatocellular carcinoma
arms.text: Five fractions of 50, 45, 40, 35, 30, or 27.5 Gy, over 5-15 days.

arms.label: Liver metastases
arms.text: Preferably three fractions (54, 51, 48, 45, or 42 Gy on alternate days) or five fractions (60, 55, 50, 45, or 40 Gy).

schema.note: Dose levels are prescription options, not randomized arms.

NCT02984566.schema_source: The open-access TROG 17.03 LARK protocol (PMID 33941111) states the single-arm liver SABR dose menus used with kilovoltage intrafraction monitoring.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Breast, prostate, or non-small cell lung cancer with up to three bone-only metastases.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Randomization is 1:1, stratified by synchronous versus metachronous metastases and by primary site (prostate, breast, or lung).

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Standard systemic treatment is given in both arms. For SBRT, acceptable regimens are 35 Gy in 7 fractions or 27 Gy in 3 fractions, depending on site and normal-tissue constraints.

arms.label: Standard care plus SBRT
arms.text: Systemic standard of care plus SBRT to all bone metastases.

arms.label: Standard care
arms.text: Systemic standard of care without SBRT.

NCT03143322.schema_source: The open-access STEREO-OS protocol (PMID 33541288) states randomization to standard care with or without bone SBRT and the stratification.
eligibility: Breast, prostate, or non-small cell lung cancer with up to 3 bone-only metastases on NaF PET or conventional SPECT-CT, plus spinal MRI if spinal disease is seen on NaF PET.
Prostate and breast patients remain eligible if hormonal treatment started within 6 months before enrollment.

Excluded: more than 3 bone metastases, a bone metastasis needing surgery such as cord compression or fracture, previous cancer within 5 years except basal cell skin cancer or in situ cervical cancer, and prior radiotherapy to a bone metastasis.

pretreatment.item: History and examination
pretreatment.note: Complete history and physical examination are required before randomization.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Unresectable esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, stage IIA-IVB (UICC 2002; stage IVB only for supraclavicular or celiac nodes).

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Randomization is 1:1, stratified by disease stage and tumor site.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Both arms use SIB-IMRT: 50.4 Gy in 28 fractions of 1.8 Gy to the planning target volume and 59.92 Gy in 28 fractions of 2.14 Gy to the planning gross tumor volume.

arms.label: SIB alone
arms.text: Radiotherapy without concurrent chemotherapy.

arms.label: SIB plus chemotherapy
arms.text: The same radiotherapy plus weekly paclitaxel 45-60 mg/m2 and a platinum agent (nedaplatin, lobaplatin, or cisplatin) 20-25 mg/m2 for 5-6 weeks. Consolidation chemotherapy is recommended for fit patients.

NCT03308552.schema_source: The open-access 3JECROG P-02 protocol (PMID 32962674) states SIB radiotherapy with or without weekly paclitaxel and platinum.
eligibility: Younger than 70 years. Histologically proven unresectable esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, stage T2 to 4 N0 to 1 M1a (UICC 2002), with stage IVB limited to supraclavicular or celiac nodes. No treatment before enrollment.
Karnofsky performance status at least 70 or ECOG 0 or 1, and Charlson comorbidity index 3 or lower.

Excluded: age 70 or older or younger than 18, prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy, pregnancy or lactation, known drug allergy, refusal of consent, or insufficient hepatic, renal, or blood counts as defined in the protocol.

pretreatment.item: Simulation
pretreatment.note: Contrast CT for positioning. GTV-T uses examination, contrast study, endoscopy, endoscopic ultrasound, neck, chest, and upper abdominal CT or MRI, and PET-CT if necessary.

during.window: At least three times in week 1, then weekly
during.note: Cone-beam CT. For elective nodal irradiation the CTV is GTV plus 3.0 to 5.0 cm craniocaudally and 0.6 to 0.8 cm laterally, plus the draining nodal region. The alternate CTV description adds a 1.0 to 1.5 cm margin on GTV-N.

schema.label: Radiotherapy
schema.text: Eligible patients aged 18 years or older with an average pain level of 5–10 on the Brief Pain Inventory short form (BPI-SF), an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status score of 0–2, and either pancreatic cancer or other tumours involving the celiac axis, received a single fraction of 25 Gy of externalbeam photons to the celiac plexus.

NCT03323489.schema_source: Lawrence et al., The Lancet. Oncology 2024 (PMID 39029483). The full text was read.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Intraprostatic recurrence only at least 2 years after external radiotherapy, Phoenix definition, stage T1-T2, PSA 10 ng/mL or less, PSA doubling time longer than 10 months, and no pelvic or metastatic disease on choline or PSMA PET.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Phase I selects one salvage SBRT schedule with a time-to-event continual reassessment method, using grade 3 or higher gastrointestinal or urinary toxicity, or any grade 4 event, within 18 weeks. Phase II then tests that selected schedule as a single arm. Five or six fractions are given over a maximum of 12 days.

arms.label: 5 x 6 Gy
arms.text: Candidate schedule, 30 Gy in five fractions.

arms.label: 6 x 6 Gy
arms.text: Candidate schedule, 36 Gy in six fractions.

arms.label: 5 x 5 Gy
arms.text: Candidate schedule, 25 Gy in five fractions.

schema.note: The three schedules are dose-finding options. Patients are not randomized among them in parallel.

NCT03438552.schema_source: The open-access GETUG-AFU 31 protocol (PMID 31377694) states the salvage prostate SBRT dose levels selected by continual reassessment.
eligibility: Biochemical recurrence at least 2 years after external radiotherapy for prostate adenocarcinoma, Phoenix definition (nadir plus 2 ng/mL). Initial stage T1 to T2c, PSA 20 ng/mL or lower, and Gleason score 7 or lower.

At relapse: clinical T1 to T2, PSA 10 ng/mL or lower, PSA doubling time longer than 10 months, WHO performance status 0 or 1, estimated CTV-to-prostate volume ratio below 0.5, multiparametric MRI, and no pelvic or metastatic disease on choline or PSMA PET. Unilateral T3a on MRI is allowed except posteriorly against the rectum.
Histologically proven intraprostatic recurrence. Seminal vesicle biopsies are optional.

followup.item: Toxicity and quality of life
followup.window: 18 weeks for dose-limiting toxicity, then 3 and 5 years
followup.note: Acute and late genitourinary and gastrointestinal toxicity over 3 years use CTCAE v4.03, with IPSS and the International Index of Erectile Function. Patients are followed for 5 years after salvage SBRT for late toxicity.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Clinically node-positive breast cancer. Tailored axillary surgery removes the sentinel nodes, palpable disease, and the clipped biopsy-positive node.

schema.text: Randomization is 1:1 by minimization. Everyone receives whole-breast radiotherapy after breast conservation or chest-wall radiotherapy after mastectomy, plus regional nodal radiotherapy. Breast or chest wall and regional nodes: 50 Gy in 25 fractions, 50.4 Gy in 28 fractions, or a hypofractionated 40 Gy in 15 fractions.

arms.label: TAS plus dissection
arms.text: Tailored axillary surgery, then axillary dissection, with nodal radiotherapy excluding the dissected axilla (levels II/III, medial supraclavicular, and internal mammary nodes).

arms.label: TAS plus full axillary radiotherapy
arms.text: Tailored axillary surgery without axillary dissection, with nodal radiotherapy including the full axilla (levels I-III, medial supraclavicular, and internal mammary nodes).

schema.note: The protocol names minimization factors but the factor list is not printed in the open text.

NCT03513614.schema_source: The open-access TAXIS protocol (PMID 30514362) states tailored axillary surgery with or without axillary dissection and the nodal radiotherapy volumes.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: PEACE V–STORM is a phase 2, open-label, randomised, controlled trial conducted in 21 hospitals in Australia, Belgium, Italy, Norway, Spain, and Switzerland.

schema.text: Patients in the MDT group had salvage lymph node dissection or stereotactic body radiotherapy (30 Gy in three fractions every other day), with 6 months of androgen deprivation therapy.

schema.label: Radiotherapy
schema.text: Patients in the ENRT group received a 45 Gy dose in 25 fractions to the pelvis with a simultaneous integrated boost of 65 Gy to the PET-positive nodes or salvage lymph node dissection, with 6 months of androgen deprivation therapy.

schema.text: Patients with bone metastases for whom the radiation oncologist prescribes either 8 Gy in 1 fraction or 20 Gy in 5 fractions. The trial is aimed at metastases in the lower spine and pelvis.

schema.text: Randomization is 1:1, stratified by prescribed dose: 8 Gy in 1 fraction versus 20 Gy in 5 fractions.

eligibility: Women age 18 to 70 with histologically confirmed invasive breast cancer, ECOG 0 to 2, able to tolerate radiotherapy, and willing to be followed.

Total mastectomy and axillary dissection of at least 10 nodes with negative margins. No one-stage reconstruction. Sentinel biopsy alone, or internal mammary dissection or sentinel biopsy, is excluded.

Node risk: at least 4 positive axillary nodes; or 1 to 3 positive nodes and T3 to 4; or 1 to 3 positive nodes and T1 to 2 with a high-risk score of at least 3 (age 40 or younger, inner quadrant, 2 to 3 positive nodes, lymphovascular invasion, and stage points as specified); or ypN+ after neoadjuvant chemotherapy.

No imaging evidence of supraclavicular or internal mammary metastases before and after systemic therapy, and no distant metastases. Internal mammary nodes must have been imaged before systemic therapy.
At least six cycles of anthracycline and/or taxane chemotherapy. Endocrine therapy for 5 years and anti-HER2 therapy for 1 year are anticipated when indicated. LVEF at least 50 percent.

Excluded: bilateral breast cancer, severe cardiac insufficiency, myocardial infarction or uncorrected unstable arrhythmia or unstable angina in the last 3 months, pericardial disease, prior chest wall or supraclavicular radiotherapy, and another malignancy except non-melanoma skin cancer, papillary or follicular thyroid carcinoma, cervical carcinoma in situ, or contralateral noninvasive breast cancer.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Investigator-initiated, two-site, open-label phase 2 randomized trial (MC1631) of pencil-beam scanning proton postmastectomy radiotherapy. Primary endpoint is the 24-month complication rate. The design assumed a 10 percent rate with conventional fractionation and treated a 10 percent absolute increase as acceptable. The published sentence that says non-inferiority is not ruled out when the upper confidence bound is greater than 10 percent conflicts with that margin, so it is not used as the decision rule. Sample size was 72 evaluable patients, inflated to 88.

schema.label: Volumes and constraints
schema.text: CTV is chest wall (and expander, implant, or autologous mound when reconstructed), axilla levels 1 to 3, supraclavicular nodes, and internal mammary nodes. Chest wall CTV stops at the anterior ribs and intercostal muscles unless those structures are involved, and it excludes the first 3 mm under the skin. Internal mammary CTV is a 4 to 5 mm expansion on the vessels from the fourth rib to the caudal supraclavicular volume. Two or three anterior fields are angled 45 to 60 degrees apart. Coverage goal is CTV D95 at least 95 percent and D0.01 cm3 at most 110 percent. Ipsilateral lung V40 percent of prescription is at most 15 percent, mean heart dose is at most 1.5 percent of prescription, brachial plexus D0.01 cm3 is at most 102 percent, and esophagus D1 cm3 is at most 72 percent. Skin objectives are also specified. A nodal boost is allowed for undissected, clinically involved internal mammary, infraclavicular, or supraclavicular nodes. A chest wall boost is not allowed.

schema.label: Systemic therapy
schema.text: Chemotherapy, when used, is typically a taxane with or without an anthracycline. Endocrine therapy is tamoxifen or an aromatase inhibitor, with ovarian suppression when appropriate. Concurrent endocrine therapy and HER2-directed therapy are allowed. Concurrent chemotherapy is not.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Multicenter randomized phase 2 trial of local consolidative therapy for oligometastatic non-small cell lung cancer that has not progressed after front-line systemic therapy. Primary endpoint is progression-free survival. The plan was 94 randomized patients, with an interim analysis at 44 events.

schema.label: Balance
schema.text: Open-label randomization was balanced dynamically on number of disease sites (0 to 1 versus 2 to 3), response to first-line therapy (stable disease versus partial response), central nervous system metastases, intrathoracic nodal status (N0 or N1 versus N2 or N3), and EGFR or ALK status.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Local consolidative therapy with or without maintenance, versus maintenance or observation. Local therapy is surgery, radiotherapy, or both, with intent to ablate all residual primary, nodal, and metastatic disease. Dose and fractionation are chosen by the treating radiation oncologist. Stereotactic ablative radiotherapy, intermediate hypofractionation (the paper gives 15 fractions to the mediastinum as an example), and concurrent chemoradiation are allowed. No single protocol dose is prescribed.

arms.label: Local consolidative therapy
arms.text: Ablation of all residual disease, then maintenance or observation at the physician's discretion.

arms.label: Maintenance or observation
arms.text: Observation is surveillance without cytotoxic therapy. Recommended maintenance options include pemetrexed, bevacizumab for non-squamous disease, erlotinib, crizotinib for ALK rearrangement, and observation. Crossover to local therapy is allowed at progression.

NCT01725165.schema_source: Gomez et al., The Lancet. Oncology 2016 (PMID 27789196). The full text was read.
eligibility: Pathologically confirmed stage IV non-small cell lung cancer, AJCC 7th edition, age 18 or older, ECOG 0 to 2, and at most 3 metastases after front-line therapy, not counting the primary tumor.

Front-line therapy is at least 4 cycles of a platinum doublet, or at least 3 months of an EGFR inhibitor for an EGFR mutation, or at least 3 months of crizotinib for an ALK rearrangement. Bevacizumab is not allowed within 2 weeks before radiotherapy.

Lesions are counted after front-line therapy. Lesions that are no longer visible or are no longer avid are not counted. Thoracic nodes from N1 to N3, including supraclavicular fossae, count as one lesion. Immediate local therapy for central nervous system lesions is allowed before randomization, and those treated lesions still count.

A complete response with nothing left to ablate is not eligible. Malignant pleural effusion or uncontrolled third-space fluid is excluded, as is uncontrolled angina, arrhythmia, or congestive heart failure. Metachronous metastases are not expressly excluded.

Recommended, not required, laboratories within 3 weeks: neutrophils at least 1,500/mm3, platelets at least 100,000/mm3, white cells at least 3,000/mm3, hemoglobin at least 9 g/dL, bilirubin at most 1.5 times the upper limit of normal, and alkaline phosphatase, AST, and ALT at most 2.5 times the upper limit, or 5 times if liver metastases are present.

followup.window: Every 6 weeks, plus or minus 2 weeks, for the first year, then at physician discretion
followup.note: CT or PET/CT. Brain MRI or CT if intracranial metastases were present. Progression uses RECIST.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: The SABR-COMET-10 trial is a multicenter, international phase III trial that aims to accrue 159 patients with 4–10 metastases, randomized to standard of care versus standard of care plus SABR to all metastatic lesions.

arms.label: Assignment

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Randomised, open-label phase 3 trial (DFCI 05-001) at 11 consortium sites in the United States and Canada. Eligible patients were aged 1 to 18 years with newly diagnosed acute lymphoblastic leukaemia. Patients were assigned to an initial risk group on the basis of baseline characteristics and received 32 days of induction. Those in complete remission were assigned to a final risk group and were eligible for the randomised comparison, which began at week 7. The primary endpoint of the randomised comparison was the overall frequency of asparaginase-related toxicities, defined as allergy, pancreatitis, and thrombotic or bleeding complications.

schema.label: Randomize

arms.label: Intramuscular native E. coli L-asparaginase

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Multi-institutional phase II trial of total neoadjuvant therapy and selective nonoperative management for MRI-staged stage II or III rectal adenocarcinoma amenable to total mesorectal excision. Both arms receive 5-FU or capecitabine-based chemoradiation. After neoadjuvant therapy, patients are restaged. Residual tumor at the primary site is treated with total mesorectal excision, and a clinical complete response is managed nonoperatively. The trial compares 3-year disease-free survival.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Noncontrolled, single-arm phase 2 protocol for patients older than 18 years with high-grade soft tissue sarcomas of the girdles or extremities. Three neoadjuvant cycles of ifosfamide and doxorubicin are given. Hypofractionated radiotherapy, 25 Gy in 5 fractions over 5 days, is given in the second cycle, and that cycle is doxorubicin only. After surgery, patients whose specimen contains less than 30% viable cells receive three additional full chemotherapy cycles.

eligibility: Age 18 to 75. Nonmetastatic high-grade soft tissue sarcoma of an extremity, or the pelvic or shoulder girdle, confirmed by pathology.
Primary or recurrent tumor that cannot be resected with a 1.0 to 2.0 cm three-dimensional margin, or for which limb preservation is not possible. No prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy.

Karnofsky index above 70 percent. Leukocytes above 3500/mm3, neutrophils above 1500/mm3, platelets above 100,000/mm3, creatinine below 1.5 mg/dL, bilirubin within normal limits, transaminases at most twice normal, and no coronary disease by ejection fraction.
Excluded: embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma, primitive neuroectodermal tumor, chondrosarcoma, osteosarcoma, HIV, pelvic or thoracic organs in the radiation field, and refusal of consent.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: CPT-SIOP-2000 was an international registry of choroid plexus tumors that nested a chemotherapy randomization for high-risk disease. High risk was defined as choroid plexus carcinoma, incompletely resected atypical choroid plexus papilloma, and all metastatic choroid plexus tumors. Patients older than 3 years were recommended to receive irradiation: focal fields for nonmetastatic choroid plexus carcinoma, incompletely resected atypical choroid plexus papilloma, or metastatic choroid plexus papilloma, and craniospinal fields for metastatic carcinoma or atypical papilloma and for carcinoma that did not respond.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Prospective, international, open-label, randomized non-inferiority trial after breast-conserving surgery for low-risk estrogen receptor-positive ductal carcinoma in situ. Eligible features were age older than 40 years, low risk of a BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation, mammographically detected unicentric non-mass lesions, low or intermediate grade without comedo or necrosis, size less than 2.5 cm, margins of at least 3 mm, and estrogen receptor-positive disease. The plan was 405 patients in each arm, allowing that about 5% would not tolerate tamoxifen and would receive radiotherapy, with a non-inferiority margin within a 5% difference in ipsilateral breast tumor recurrence and 90% power. Primary endpoints are ipsilateral, regional, contralateral, and distant recurrence of ductal carcinoma in situ or invasive cancer.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Randomization is stratified by the Taiwan Breast Cancer Consortium.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients are randomized 1:1 to low-dose tamoxifen or radiotherapy.

arms.label: Radiotherapy

eligibility: New histologic DCIS after breast-conserving surgery. Age at least 40. Manchester score below 10. Known BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation is excluded.
Mammographically detected, unicentric, non-mass, nonpalpable lesion. No bloody nipple discharge. Clinically node negative.
Low or intermediate nuclear grade without comedo or necrosis. Size at most 2.5 cm. Ink margin at least 3 mm. ER positive in at least 10 percent of tumor cells.
Excluded: palpable, multicentric, mass-like, or high-grade DCIS, margin under 3 mm, mastectomy, and another neoplasm within 5 years except CIN1 or localized non-melanoma skin cancer.

schema.text: Two subsets. N0 is no regional nodal involvement, N1 is regional nodal involvement, and Nx is nodal status unknown. VA is vincristine and actinomycin.

schema.text: Single-center, open-label, single-arm phase II trial of TheraSphere selective internal radiation therapy for inoperable liver-dominant metastatic neuroendocrine neoplasia. Twenty-four patients who pass pre-SIRT workup are treated. Three extra patients may be recruited for dropout.

schema.text: One treatment with TheraSphere SIRT. Activity is chosen after the angiogram and Tc-99m MAA shunt study. A fixed gray dose is not printed.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Prospective single-arm phase II trial of SABR for T1-2 N0 M0 non-small cell lung cancer with fibrotic interstitial lung disease. Target accrual 39. Analysis is stratified into three ILD-GAP cohorts.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Patients are divided into three cohorts by the ILD-GAP index. This is not a randomized comparison.

schema.label: Regimen
schema.text: Starting dose is standard SABR, with up to two prespecified de-escalations if grade 5 toxicity occurs in 2 or more of the first 7 patients in a cohort, or in 2 or more of the first 7 patients with a specific ILD subtype, within 6 months.

arms.label: SABR
arms.text: Start at 50 Gy in 5 fractions every other day. First de-escalation: 50 Gy in 10 daily fractions. Second: 45 Gy in 15 daily fractions.

NCT03485378.schema_source: Open-access protocol, Palma et al., BMC Cancer 2019 (PMID 31829203). Read from the full text.
eligibility: AJCC 8th edition T1-2 N0 M0, tumor 5 cm or smaller, not a surgical candidate (surgeon consultation, multidisciplinary conference, or patient refusal).
Pathologic confirmation is strongly recommended. If biopsy risk is unacceptable, growth on CT and/or FDG avidity strongly suggestive of NSCLC is accepted.
ECOG 0 to 3, age at least 18, life expectancy above 6 months. Fibrotic ILD of any subtype diagnosed by a pulmonologist and confirmed by central review.

Excluded: prior invasive malignancy unless disease free at least 2 years (non-melanoma skin cancer excepted), prior thoracic radiotherapy, planned other local or systemic anticancer therapy except at progression, pregnancy, and concurrent known radiosensitizers such as methotrexate. Antifibrotics and steroids for ILD may continue. Other immunosuppressants stop for 2 weeks before and after SABR.

pretreatment.item: Staging and ILD review
pretreatment.note: History and physical, pulmonology assessment, central ILD review, PET/CT, HRCT, and pulmonary function tests. Brain MRI if symptoms. Mediastinal sampling is allowed but not required. Nodes 1 cm or smaller without pathologic PET uptake are N0. Larger or PET-avid nodes may remain eligible if biopsy is negative.

followup.item: Oncology review
followup.window: 3, 6, 9, and 12 months, then 18 and 24 months, then annually through year 5

followup.window: HRCT at 3, 6, 12, 18, and 24 months, then annually. PFTs at 6, 12, 18, and 24 months, then annually
followup.note: Pulmonology at least every 6 months in year 1 and at least annually in years 2 to 5. Outside PFTs within 2 months of the due date are acceptable. Patients who decline SABR may consent to phone calls every 3 months for 2 years.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Multicenter single-arm phase II trial for treatment-naive limited-stage small cell lung cancer. Planned 55 patients.

schema.label: Regimen
schema.text: Four cycles of platinum-etoposide, concurrent thoracic radiotherapy, prophylactic cranial irradiation if no progression, then serplulimab.

arms.label: Chemoradiotherapy then serplulimab
arms.text: Etoposide 100 mg/m2 intravenously on days 1 to 3 with cisplatin 75 mg/m2 on day 1, or carboplatin AUC 5, every 3 weeks, for four cycles. Thoracic radiotherapy starts no later than after two chemotherapy cycles: 45 Gy in 15 fractions of 3 Gy over 3 weeks to the primary tumor and involved mediastinal nodes. PCI, if no progression, is 25 Gy in 10 fractions over 2 weeks. Then serplulimab 300 mg intravenously every 3 weeks for up to 1 year, until progression, intolerable toxicity, or withdrawal. Dose reduction of serplulimab is not permitted.

NCT05443646.schema_source: Open-access protocol, Wu et al., BMJ Open 2025 (PMID 40398957). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Age 18 to 75, ECOG 0 or 1, histologically or cytologically confirmed limited-stage SCLC, at least one RECIST 1.1 evaluable lesion, and no serious hematopoietic, cardiac, hepatic, renal, or immune abnormality. Patients suitable for surgery who refuse surgery are included. PD-L1 testing is recommended but not required.
Table 1 also lists exclusions. The extracted exclusion lines are truncated, so only the inclusion items above are restated.

pretreatment.item: Simulation
pretreatment.note: 4D-CT and contrast CT when possible, 0.3 cm slices. Organ constraints include lung V20 below 25%, mean lung dose at most 15 Gy, spinal cord PRV Dmax below 42 Gy, esophagus Dmax below 50 Gy and mean below 34 Gy, heart V30 below 50%, and hippocampus constraints.

during.window: Every 4 cycles during serplulimab, then every 6 weeks for the first 48 weeks and every 9 weeks after that
during.note: Chest CT and brain MRI, with ultrasound if needed. Contrast CT of neck, thorax, and abdomen is preferred. Brain CT or PET is allowed if MRI is contraindicated. Adverse events at each visit using CTCAE v5.0. A phone interview 1 to 2 weeks after drug delivery.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Open-label, single-arm, multicenter phase II trial using Simon's two-stage design for locally advanced, potentially resectable rectal adenocarcinoma. Target 44 patients. If 2 or fewer pathologic complete responses occur in the first 13 patients, the study stops.

schema.label: Regimen
schema.text: Short-course radiotherapy, then mFOLFOX-6 plus avelumab, then total mesorectal excision around week 16.

arms.label: SCRT, mFOLFOX-6, avelumab, TME
arms.text: 25 Gy in 5 fractions. Two weeks later, avelumab 10 mg/kg then mFOLFOX-6 30 minutes later, every 2 weeks for 6 cycles. TME (open, laparoscopic, or robotic) about week 16.

NCT03503630.schema_source: Open-access protocol, Shamseddine et al., BMC Cancer 2020 (PMID 32873251). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Age at least 18, signed consent, cT2 N1-3 or cT3/T4a N0-3, within 12 cm of the anal verge, histologically proven rectal adenocarcinoma, ECOG 0 or 1.

ANC at least 1.5 x 10^9/L, platelets at least 100 x 10^9/L, hemoglobin at least 9 g/dL, bilirubin at most 1.5 times ULN, AST and ALT at most 2.5 times ULN (5 times if liver metastases), creatinine clearance at least 30 mL/min. The remainder of Table 1 is truncated in the extract and is not invented.

pretreatment.item: Visit 1
pretreatment.note: Consent, medical history, complete physical examination including digital rectal examination, FACT-C, and baseline laboratories.

followup.item: After surgery
followup.window: Every 3 months for 3 years
followup.note: Participation is 36 months, with 16 weeks of treatment and 3 years of postoperative follow-up.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Randomized phase 3 trial for children and young adults under 30 years with high-risk neuroblastoma, enrolled 16 March 2001 to 24 February 2006.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Blocks stratified by INSS stage, age (under 365 days or 365 days and older), MYCN amplification, and INPC favorable or unfavorable histology.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: 1:1 web-based randomization at diagnosis, open label. All patients receive six induction cycles, myeloablative consolidation, radiotherapy to the primary site and MIBG-avid metastases present before myeloablation, then oral isotretinoin. PBSC are collected after two induction cycles. Radiotherapy dose is not stated.

arms.label: Purged PBSC
arms.text: Immunomagnetic purge: carbonyl iron and magnet removal of phagocytes, then beads with five anti-neuroblastoma antibodies.

arms.label: Non-purged PBSC
arms.text: Unpurged peripheral blood stem cells for autologous transplant after six induction cycles.

NCT00004188.schema_source: Trial report, Kreissman et al., The Lancet Oncology 2013 (PMID 23890779). Read from the full text.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Multi-institutional, open-label, single-arm phase 2 trial (ACOSOG Z6041) of neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy and local excision for clinical T2N0 distal rectal cancer.

schema.label: Regimen
schema.text: The original regimen was revised after 53 patients because of toxicity. Oxaliplatin dose did not change.

arms.label: Chemoradiotherapy then local excision
arms.text: Original: capecitabine 825 mg/m2 twice daily on days 1 to 14 and 22 to 35, oxaliplatin 50 mg/m2 in weeks 1, 2, 4, and 5, and 1.8 Gy per day, 5 days per week, to 45 Gy then a boost to 54 Gy (PTV2 is GTV plus 2 cm). Revised: capecitabine 725 mg/m2 twice daily, 5 days per week for 5 weeks, total dose 50.4 Gy, same oxaliplatin. Local excision 4 to 8 weeks later, transanal or TEM, full thickness with a 1 cm margin.

NCT00114231.schema_source: Trial report, Garcia-Aguilar et al., The Lancet Oncology 2015 (PMID 26474521). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Clinical T2N0 rectal adenocarcinoma on endorectal ultrasound or endorectal-coil MRI, less than 4 cm, less than 40% of the circumference, within 8 cm of the anal verge, ECOG at most 2.
Colonoscopy, rigid proctoscopy, digital exam, CT of the abdomen and pelvis, and chest radiograph or CT. Tumors fixed to adjacent structures are ineligible.

followup.item: Anorectal function and quality of life
followup.window: Baseline and 1 year after surgery
followup.note: Validated instruments. Recurrence and survival were assessed at scheduled intervals. The interval list was not in the sections read.

submission.label: Data
submission.text: Data were submitted to the ACOSOG statistical center.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-institution, nonrandomized FLARE-RT study. Forty-nine patients with AJCC 7 stage IIB to IIIB NSCLC, or N2 recurrence without prior chemoradiation, enrolled 2016 to 2021 and started chemoradiation. Assignment used week-3 FDG-PET, not randomization.

schema.label: Assign
schema.text: Concurrent chemotherapy was carboplatin-paclitaxel, cisplatin-etoposide (printed as etopside), or another platinum doublet. Consolidation chemotherapy or an immune checkpoint inhibitor was allowed. Mid-treatment FDG-PET was done in week 3, after 24 Gy.

arms.label: PET response
arms.text: Continued 60 Gy in 30 fractions.

arms.label: PET nonresponse
arms.text: Concomitant integral boost of 14 Gy in 15 fractions to residual metabolic disease, for a total integral dose of 74 Gy.

NCT02773238.schema_source: Trial report, Zeng et al., Clinical Cancer Research 2026 (PMID 42207168). Read from the full text.
eligibility: AJCC 7 stage IIB to IIIB NSCLC, or N2 recurrence without prior chemoradiation. Patients who enrolled but never started chemoradiation were excluded from this analysis.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: COG AREN0533 for favorable-histology Wilms tumor with extrapulmonary metastases, with or without lung metastases. Enrollment February 2007 to May 2013 after central review and risk assignment on AREN03B2.

schema.label: Regimen
schema.text: Six weeks of induction DD-4A (vincristine, dactinomycin, and doxorubicin), then regimen M in weeks 7 to 33, adding four cycles of cyclophosphamide and etoposide to a modified DD-4A backbone. Drug doses and radiotherapy gray are not stated in this report.

schema.label: Radiotherapy
schema.text: Protocol-recommended radiotherapy included metastatic sites, and flank or whole-abdominal radiotherapy for local stage III. Liver radiotherapy was indicated for liver metastases except a solitary liver lesion resected with negative margins before chemotherapy. Patients with extrapulmonary and lung metastases received whole-lung irradiation.

schema.label: Surgery
schema.text: Biopsy or resection of suspicious abdominal or liver sites at the initial exploration. Residual intra-abdominal metastatic disease at the week-6 evaluation was to be resected when complete resection was feasible; otherwise resection was reassessed at the end of therapy.

NCT00379340.schema_source: Trial report, Benedetti et al., Cancer 2024 (PMID 37933882). Read from the full text.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Prospective phase II, nonrandomized, multicenter ACCESS trial. Two adult strata, myeloablative conditioning and reduced-intensity or nonmyeloablative conditioning, before peripheral-blood stem-cell transplantation from a mismatched unrelated donor. GVHD prophylaxis was cyclophosphamide, tacrolimus, and mycophenolate mofetil. Conditioning drug doses are not stated in the sections read.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Analyzed separately for myeloablative and reduced-intensity or nonmyeloablative conditioning. Primary objective is 1-year overall survival in each stratum.

NCT04904588.schema_source: Trial report, Al Malki et al., Journal of Clinical Oncology 2025 (PMID 40523209). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Age at least 18 years, first allogeneic transplant. Myeloablative recipients had to be younger than 66 years with HCT-CI below 5.
Acute or chronic leukemia without circulating blasts and with marrow blasts below 5%, myelodysplastic syndrome, or lymphoma in remission. Myelofibrosis was excluded.
No suitable HLA-identical sibling or matched unrelated donor. Mismatched unrelated donors were HLA matched at 4/8 to 7/8 (A, B, C, and DRB1), age 18 to 35 years, and considered eligible to donate.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: ACOSOG Z0010, a prospective observational study of breast-conserving therapy and sentinel-node dissection. Clinicians were blinded to sentinel-node and bone-marrow immunohistochemistry.

schema.label: Intervention
schema.text: Lumpectomy and sentinel-node dissection. Bilateral anterior iliac-crest bone marrow aspiration was optional before March 2001 and then required, immediately before the breast operation. Whole-breast irradiation excluded a third supraclavicular field: 45 to 50 Gy in tangential fields with coplanar posterior borders. Adjuvant systemic therapy was chosen by the treating clinician.

NCT00003854.schema_source: Trial report, Giuliano et al., JAMA 2011 (PMID 21791687). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Clinical T1 to T2, N0, M0 invasive breast carcinoma planned for breast-conserving therapy. Negative pregnancy test and ECOG/Zubrod score 2 or lower.
Excluded: neoadjuvant therapy, prepectoral implants, concurrent bilateral malignancies, disease not amenable to lumpectomy, or previous axillary surgery.

pretreatment.item: Surgeon credentialing
pretreatment.note: Twenty consecutive sentinel-node procedures with identification and accuracy at least 85% based on completion dissection, or a postgraduate sentinel-node program.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Phase 3 trial designed for overall survival in 900 men with high-risk prostate cancer. Accrual stopped early when orteronel development ended, and the trial was redesigned around a composite biochemical failure endpoint.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Risk criteria, type of radiotherapy boost, and whether androgen deprivation started before or after enrollment.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: 1:1 to standard therapy or standard therapy plus orteronel. Radiotherapy used at least 6 MV photons, IMRT to the pelvis 45 Gy in 25 fractions, then an IMRT boost of 34.2 Gy in 19 fractions or an LDR or HDR brachytherapy boost. PTV margins on pelvic and prostate CTVs were 0.5 to 1.0 cm. Daily image guidance was required. Androgen deprivation was a GnRH agonist for 24 months plus an oral antiandrogen through the end of radiotherapy.

arms.label: Standard therapy
arms.text: Androgen deprivation for 8 weeks, then dose-escalated radiotherapy with concurrent and adjuvant androgen deprivation for 24 months total.

arms.label: Standard therapy plus orteronel
arms.text: The same treatment plus orteronel 300 mg orally twice daily from enrollment for 2 years.

NCT01546987.schema_source: Trial report, Hamstra et al., International Journal of Radiation Oncology, Biology, Physics 2025 (PMID 40712984). Read from the full text.
eligibility: One of: Gleason 9 or higher and PSA at most 150, any T stage; Gleason 8, PSA below 20, and T2 or higher; Gleason 8 and PSA 20 to 150, any T stage; or Gleason 7 and PSA 20 to 150, any T stage.
No nodal or distant metastasis on axial imaging and bone scan, Zubrod 0 or 1, and adequate laboratories. Prior androgen deprivation was allowed if it began within 50 days of registration.

followup.item: Clinical assessment
followup.window: Every 3 months for 2 years, every 6 months for the next 3 years, then annually
followup.note: Testosterone was collected through 5 years. Lipids, hemoglobin A1c, and fasting glucose at baseline, 12 months, and 24 months. Body mass index at baseline and annually.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: COG AEWS02P1, a single-arm pilot for newly diagnosed metastatic Ewing sarcoma. Fourteen cycles: induction (first four cycles), local control usually from week 13, then consolidation (10 cycles).

schema.label: Regimen
schema.text: Cycles A and B alternated every 3 weeks. Cycle A: vincristine 1.5 mg/m2 on day 1, doxorubicin 37.5 mg/m2/day on days 1 and 2, and cyclophosphamide 1200 mg/m2 on day 1. Cycle B: ifosfamide 1800 mg/m2/day and etoposide 100 mg/m2/day on days 1 to 5. MESNA with cyclophosphamide and ifosfamide, and G-CSF after each cycle. Vinblastine and celecoxib were given concomitantly; their doses are not stated in the sections read. Local control was surgery, radiotherapy, or both, by institutional preference. Radiotherapy dose is not stated.

NCT00061893.schema_source: Trial report, Felgenhauer et al., Pediatric Blood & Cancer 2012 (PMID 23065953). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Age under 50 years, newly diagnosed Ewing sarcoma of bone or soft tissue metastatic to bone and/or bone marrow, body surface area at least 0.4 m2, adequate renal, hepatic, and cardiac function, and Karnofsky or Lansky score at least 50.
Lung-only metastases could enroll, but AEWS0331 had priority. Excluded: sulfa allergy, aspirin hypersensitivity, asthma triad, or a primary central nervous system lesion.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Multicenter, nonrandomized, single-arm trial at 7 U.S. centers. A safety run-in enrolled the first 6 patients, with biomarkers after one dose of sotigalimab before chemoradiation.

schema.label: Regimen
schema.text: Sotigalimab for 3 to 4 doses with weekly carboplatin and paclitaxel and radiotherapy over 5 to 6 weeks, then surgery. Radiotherapy was 5040 cGy in 28 fractions to the planning target volume, Monday through Friday. Carboplatin, paclitaxel, and sotigalimab milligram doses are not stated in the sections read.

NCT03165994.schema_source: Trial report, Ko et al., Cancer Research Communications 2025 (PMID 39907035). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Age at least 18, histologic squamous cell carcinoma, adenocarcinoma, or undifferentiated carcinoma of the esophagus or gastroesophageal junction, clinical T1 to T3 Nx by endoscopic ultrasound, ECOG 0 or 1, fit for esophagectomy, and adequate hematologic, renal, and hepatic parameters. The numeric laboratory cutoffs were truncated in the text read, so they are omitted.
Excluded: T1N0 disease, cervical esophageal tumors, invasion of the tracheobronchial tree or a tracheoesophageal fistula, and nodes outside the radiation field or not resectable at esophagectomy.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: ARO-2013-04, a multicenter prospective single-arm trial of adjuvant hypofractionated whole-breast radiotherapy with a simultaneous integrated boost after breast-conserving surgery. The hypothesis was that acute grade 2 or higher skin reaction would occur in 20% of patients or fewer.

schema.label: Regimen
schema.text: Whole breast 40 Gy in 16 fractions of 2.5 Gy, with an added 0.5 Gy per fraction to the tumor bed, for 48 Gy in 16 fractions to the boost PTV. 3D conformal radiotherapy or IMRT was allowed. The tumor bed had to be identifiable on planning CT by seroma or clips. Clips were not mandatory.

NCT01948726.schema_source: Trial report, Krug et al., Strahlentherapie und Onkologie 2020 (PMID 33001241). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Women age 18 or older with unifocal breast cancer, breast-conserving surgery with clear margins, and an indication for whole-breast radiotherapy without regional nodes plus a tumor-bed boost. Prior adjuvant or neoadjuvant chemotherapy was allowed. Endocrine therapy was allowed during radiotherapy.

Excluded: mastectomy, no indication for a boost, tumor bed not identifiable on planning CT, extensive seroma requiring an excessive boost, indication for regional-node irradiation, previous chest radiotherapy, or comorbidity that precluded protocol radiotherapy.

pretreatment.item: History and examination
pretreatment.note: Staging followed national and international breast cancer guidelines. The tumor bed had to be visible on the planning CT.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-arm phase 2 trial, June 2013 to October 2014, 50 patients after mastectomy or breast-conserving surgery, of whom 10 had breast-conserving surgery.

schema.label: Regimen
schema.text: 2D planning with two tangential fields and an incident supraclavicular field. 34 Gy in 10 fractions over 2 weeks, prescribed at mid-separation. Supraclavicular dose was prescribed at dmax on cobalt or a 6 MV linac. Internal mammary nodes were not treated and no cardiac shielding was used. Breast-conserving cases were treated on a 6 MV linac with a 30 degree wedge and a boost of 10 Gy in 5 fractions over 1 week with photons or electrons.

NCT02460744.schema_source: Trial report, Yadav et al., Reports of Practical Oncology and Radiotherapy 2021 (PMID 34434565). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Age at least 18, female or male, invasive breast carcinoma, breast-conserving surgery or mastectomy, at least 10 axillary nodes dissected, complete microscopic excision, T1 to T4 pN0 to N3 M0, neoadjuvant or adjuvant chemotherapy, and written informed consent. The eligibility sentence was truncated after consent in the text read.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: SWOG-Intergroup S0220, a single-arm feasibility study of trimodality therapy for superior sulcus NSCLC. Accrual goal 45 eligible patients.

schema.label: Regimen
schema.text: Induction cisplatin 50 mg/m2 intravenously on days 1, 8, 29, and 36, and etoposide 50 mg/m2 intravenously on days 1 to 5 and 29 to 33, with thoracic radiotherapy in 1.8 Gy fractions to 45 Gy to the primary tumor and ipsilateral supraclavicular region. Mediastinal or hilar coverage was not required. Patients without progression had thoracotomy 3 to 7 weeks later. Consolidation docetaxel was 75 mg/m2 intravenously every 21 days for three doses, starting 3 to 8 weeks after surgery or definitive radiotherapy.

NCT00062439.schema_source: Trial report, Kernstine et al., The Annals of Thoracic Surgery 2014 (PMID 24980603). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Single, previously untreated superior sulcus NSCLC, selected stage IIB (T3N0), IIIA (T3N1), or IIIB (T4N0 to N1). Apical tumor with or without Pancoast syndrome, or CT or MRI invasion of the upper chest wall, ribs 1 or 2, upper thoracic vertebral bodies, or subclavian vessels.

N2 excluded by negative mediastinoscopy or by negative mediastinal CT and PET. Metastatic workup used abdominal CT and bone scan or PET, plus brain CT or MRI. Zubrod 0 to 2, with pulmonary function and laboratories used to judge fitness.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: BMT CTN 1507, an open-label phase 2 single-arm multicenter study at 19 U.S. sites of related HLA-haploidentical bone marrow transplantation for adults with severe sickle cell disease. Enrollment October 2017 to January 2021. Primary endpoint 2-year event-free survival.

schema.label: Regimen
schema.text: Hydroxyurea 30 mg/kg/day for 60 days as preconditioning (day -70 to day -10). Conditioning: thymoglobulin 4.5 mg/kg, thiotepa 10 mg/kg, cyclophosphamide 29 mg/kg total split over 2 consecutive days, fludarabine 150 mg/m2 total over 5 consecutive days, and 200 cGy total-body irradiation. GVHD prophylaxis: cyclophosphamide 50 mg/kg on days +3 and +4, mycophenolate mofetil 15 mg/kg three times daily (maximum 3 g/day) from day +5 through day +35, and sirolimus starting at 1 mg/m2 daily (maximum 2 mg) from day +5.

NCT03263559.schema_source: Trial report, Kassim et al., NEJM Evidence 2025 (PMID 39998298). Read from the full text.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: CARTS, a nonrandomized feasibility study of chemoradiation and organ-sparing transanal endoscopic microsurgery for distal rectal adenocarcinoma. A three-step review was planned after 20, 33, and 55 patients. At least 15 Dutch hospitals were planned, including 3 university centers.

schema.label: Regimen
schema.text: Radiotherapy in 25 fractions over 5 weeks. The gray per fraction is not stated in the treatment paragraph read. Capecitabine 825 mg/m2 twice daily, 7 days per week, throughout radiotherapy. Six weeks after chemoradiation, MRI, rectoscopy, and endorectal ultrasound were used to judge response. Clinical T0 to T2 tumors underwent local excision by TEM 8 to 10 weeks after chemoradiation. All other patients underwent total mesorectal excision.

NCT01273051.schema_source: Open-access protocol, Bökkerink et al., BMC Surgery 2011 (PMID 22171697). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Distal adenocarcinoma within 10 cm of the anal verge, cT1 to T3, age older than 18, and written consent.

Excluded: low-risk T1, tumors unsuitable for TEM (circular or intra-anal), pre-existing fecal incontinence, synchronous tumors, mesorectal nodes larger than 5 mm on CT, MRI, or endorectal ultrasound, and contraindications to capecitabine.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: NRG/RTOG 0522 long-term update. Patients with oropharynx, larynx, or hypopharynx squamous carcinoma, AJCC 6 T2 N2 to N3 M0 or T3 to T4 any N M0, were enrolled and randomized 1:1. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Larynx versus non-larynx, nodes N0 versus N1 to N2b versus N2c to N3, Zubrod 0 versus 1, IMRT no versus yes, and pretreatment PET/CT no versus yes.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Cisplatin 100 mg/m2 on days 1 and 22 of radiotherapy in both arms. 3D conformal radiotherapy was 72 Gy in 42 fractions over 6 weeks, with twice-daily treatment for the last 12 treatment days. IMRT was 70 Gy in 35 fractions over 6 weeks, with twice-daily treatment once per week during weeks 2 to 6.

arms.label: Arm A
arms.text: Radiotherapy and cisplatin.

arms.label: Arm B
arms.text: The same radiotherapy and cisplatin, plus cetuximab 400 mg/m2 the week before radiotherapy and 250 mg/m2 weekly during radiotherapy.

NCT00265941.schema_source: Trial report, Caudell et al., International Journal of Radiation Oncology, Biology, Physics 2023 (PMID 36549347). Read from the full text.

followup.item: Imaging and examination
followup.window: Imaging at 8 to 9 weeks, 6 months, and then annually. Examination every 3 months for 2 years, every 6 months through year 5, then annually.
followup.note: Late reactions were scored with CTCAE version 3.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-arm phase II study of hyperthermia plus salvage chemoradiation for unresectable recurrent head and neck cancer.

schema.label: Regimen
schema.text: 10 Gy in 2 fractions to gross tumor over the first 2 weeks, then 40 Gy in 20 fractions to the clinical target volume over 4 weeks, 50 Gy in 22 fractions total. Weekly hyperthermia for 6 sessions, 40 minutes, starting within 2 hours after radiotherapy, maximum temperature 42 plus or minus 0.5 C. Weekly cisplatin 20 mg/m2 and docetaxel 10 to 12 mg/m2 for 6 weeks.

NCT02567383.schema_source: Trial report, Yang et al., Radiation Oncology 2025 (PMID 39920700). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Age 20 to 85 years, nonmetastatic recurrent head and neck cancer in a previously irradiated region, prior cumulative dose at least 40 Gy, prior radiotherapy completed at least 6 months earlier, prior fraction size 1.6 to 2.2 Gy, and not a candidate for salvage surgery.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: This paper is a literature review. It states the Alliance A011202 randomization in one sentence and does not provide eligibility, doses, or a follow-up calendar.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients with a positive sentinel node after neoadjuvant therapy were randomized to axillary dissection followed by nodal irradiation of the undissected axilla, supraclavicular fossa, and internal mammary nodes, or to no axillary dissection and radiotherapy to the axilla, supraclavicular fossa, and internal mammary nodes. Radiotherapy dose is not stated.

NCT01901094.schema_source: Trial report, Mukherjee et al., European Journal of Breast Health 2025 (PMID 41447642). Read from the full text.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-arm multicenter study of reduced-dose craniospinal irradiation for average-risk medulloblastoma. Radiotherapy starts within 4 weeks of resection.

schema.label: Radiotherapy
schema.text: 18 Gy photons to the whole brain and spine in 10 fractions, with a tumor-bed boost in 21 fractions to 55.8 Gy. Concurrent weekly vincristine 1.5 mg/m2, maximum 2 mg, for 6 doses.

schema.label: Maintenance
schema.text: Starts 4 weeks after radiotherapy. Nine cycles in an AABAABAAB pattern. Regimen A: lomustine 75 mg/m2 and cisplatin 70 mg/m2 on day 0, and vincristine 1.5 mg/m2 (maximum 2 mg) on days 0, 7, and 14. Regimen B: cyclophosphamide 1000 mg/m2 on days 0 and 1, etoposide 150 mg/m2 intravenously on days 0 and 1, then oral etoposide 50 mg/m2 on days 14 to 34.

NCT00031590.schema_source: Minturn et al., Frontiers in Oncology 2021 (PMID 34540703). The full text was read.
eligibility: Age 3 to 30 at diagnosis. Histologically proven average-risk medulloblastoma: residual tumor under 1.5 cm3, no metastases on brain and spine MRI, and negative CSF cytology.
CSF by lumbar puncture 10 days to 4 weeks after surgery. Postoperative MRI of the primary site within 72 hours, preferably within 48 hours.

followup.item: Brain and spine MRI
followup.window: Every 3 months during maintenance and the first year after treatment, every 6 months in years 2 and 3, then yearly
followup.note: Also if relapse is suspected. Adverse events use CTCAE version 3.0.

followup.item: Audiograms
followup.window: Before each chemotherapy cycle, every 6 months for 1 to 3 years after chemotherapy, then yearly

followup.item: Neurocognitive testing
followup.window: Within 6 months of diagnosis, then 1, 2, and 3 years after chemotherapy
followup.note: Age-appropriate Wechsler scales.

specimens.window: After institutional diagnosis
specimens.note: Sent to Children's Hospital of Philadelphia for correlative studies.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Memorial Sloan Kettering protocol 01-142. Four cycles of R-CHOP-14, then FDG-PET. A negative PET is followed by 3 cycles of ICE. A positive PET is followed by 2 cycles of ICE, 1 cycle of rituximab plus ICE, then carmustine, etoposide, cytarabine, and melphalan with autologous stem-cell rescue. Milligram doses are not restated in this paper.

NCT00039195.schema_source: Bantilan et al., Blood Advances 2024 (PMID 38271621). The full text was read. The schema is Memorial Sloan Kettering protocol 01-142. The same paper also reports NCT00712582.
eligibility: One to three age-adjusted IPI risk factors. Suitable for stem-cell rescue. CD20-positive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma or primary mediastinal B-cell lymphoma. Measurable disease by PET. Bone marrow involvement by small cleaved-cell lymphoma did not exclude patients.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Open-label phase I/II trial of neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy, then nelfinavir and stereotactic body radiotherapy, for non-metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma. The trial closed early when the chemotherapy backbone was no longer standard.

schema.label: Sequence
schema.text: Three 3-week cycles of gemcitabine, leucovorin, fluorouracil, and oregovomab. Milligram doses of the cytotoxic drugs were not in the sections read. Nelfinavir 1250 mg twice daily for 5 weeks, with 40 Gy in 5 fractions during the third week. Another chemoimmunotherapy cycle follows, then pancreaticoduodenectomy if resectable, then three more cycles, for 7 cycles total. If CA-125 is at least 10 units/mL, oregovomab 2 mg is given for 7 doses: 3 before radiotherapy, 1 between radiotherapy and resection, and 3 after surgery. Patients below that CA-125 level do not receive oregovomab.

schema.label: Radiotherapy
schema.text: 40 Gy in 5 daily fractions. At least 95 percent of the PTV is covered, or 93 percent if bowel constraints cannot be met. Maximum PTV dose does not exceed 110 percent. Stomach and small bowel maximum point dose is 32 Gy. Other constraints are cited from a prior study and are not restated here.

NCT01959672.schema_source: Lin et al., American journal of clinical oncology 2019 (PMID 31513018). The full text was read.
eligibility: Age 19 or older. Newly diagnosed, pathologically confirmed, non-metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma no larger than 10 cm, including resectable, borderline, and unresectable disease. Karnofsky performance status at least 60 percent and laboratories appropriate for chemotherapy. Numeric cutoffs were not in the sections read.
Biliary or gastroduodenal obstruction is allowed if drained or bypassed first. A prior malignancy is allowed if treatment finished more than 5 years earlier and there is no clinical evidence of it.

Excluded: prior radiotherapy overlapping the 20 percent isodose, contraindication to staging laparoscopy, allergy to murine protein or a protocol drug, uncontrolled intercurrent illness, autoimmune or immunodeficiency disease, inability to consent, pregnancy or nursing, contraindicated concomitant medicines, other investigational agents, and hepatic insufficiency.

pretreatment.item: History, laboratories, and imaging
pretreatment.note: Blood counts, chemistries, CA-125, and CA 19-9. Contrast CT, MRI, PET, and/or endoscopic or laparoscopic ultrasound.

pretreatment.item: Staging laparoscopy and fiducials
pretreatment.note: Confirms no peritoneal metastases. Two fiducials are placed about 2 cm apart.

during.note: Medical and radiation oncology. Toxicity uses CTCAE version 3.0.

followup.item: History, examination, CT, and laboratories
followup.window: Every 3 months in year 1, every 4 months in year 2, then twice a year
followup.note: Contrast CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis, and CA 19-9. Response uses RECIST 1.1.

specimens.item: Peripheral blood for ELISPOT and HAMA
specimens.window: Before chemotherapy, before the second infusion for the first 6 patients, before radiotherapy, before resection or restaging, and 3 weeks after cycle 7
specimens.note: Only for high CA-125. HAMA is done at a central laboratory.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Phase 2 trial of yttrium-90 ibritumomab tiuxetan with fludarabine and melphalan reduced-intensity allogeneic transplantation for high-risk B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma.

schema.label: Conditioning
schema.text: Indium-111 ibritumomab tiuxetan 5.0 mCi on day -21. Yttrium-90 ibritumomab tiuxetan 0.4 mCi/kg on day -14, using actual body weight, maximum 32 mCi. Fludarabine 25 mg/m2 daily on days -9 to -5. Melphalan 140 mg/m2 on day -4. Peripheral-blood stem cells on day 0.

schema.label: Rituximab and graft-versus-host prophylaxis
schema.text: Rituximab 250 mg/m2 on day +8 for every patient. Additional rituximab on day -21 or day -14 only if the level two days earlier was under 10 micrograms/mL, and on day +1 if it was not given on those days. The first 8 patients all received rituximab on days -21 and -14. Tacrolimus and sirolimus start on day -3. Methotrexate 10 mg/m2 on day +1 and 5 mg/m2 on days +3 and +6 may be added for unrelated donors.

NCT00577278.schema_source: Mei et al., Clinical lymphoma, myeloma & leukemia 2023 (PMID 37301631). The full text was read.
eligibility: High-risk B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma with a fully matched sibling or an 8/8 or 7/8 matched unrelated donor. A formal age and laboratory list was not in the sections read.

followup.item: Contrast CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis
followup.window: 6 weeks, 3 months, 6 months, 1 year, then yearly to 5 years
followup.note: Response uses Cheson 2007 criteria. PET/CT before transplant and at 1 year. If the pretransplant PET is positive, another PET/CT is done at 6 weeks.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: The clinical portion is a phase 1/2 trial of zoledronic acid given concurrently with hypofractionated radiotherapy and fluorouracil or capecitabine, after induction FOLFIRINOX or gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel, for borderline resectable or locally advanced pancreatic adenocarcinoma. Zoledronic acid milligrams and the radiotherapy dose are not stated in this paper.

NCT03073785.schema_source: Seshacharyulu et al., EBioMedicine 2022 (PMID 34971971). The full text was read. Most of the paper is preclinical. The clinical doses are not stated.
eligibility: Borderline resectable or locally advanced pancreatic adenocarcinoma. Written consent was obtained after induction chemotherapy. A numeric laboratory list was not in the sections read.

specimens.window: During the zoledronic acid and radiotherapy study
specimens.note: RNA sequencing for immune activation. The draw clock time is not stated.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Clinical trial with a historical control, testing a higher iodine-131 dose in severe Graves disease with a large goiter.

schema.label: Dose
schema.text: The intervention cohort received 250 microcuries of iodine-131 per mL of thyroid tissue, corrected for 24-hour uptake. The historical control, drawn from an earlier randomized trial at the same institution, received 200 microcuries per mL corrected for 24-hour uptake.

NCT01039818.schema_source: Dora et al., Journal of Thyroid Research 2013 (PMID 23984185). The full text was read.
eligibility: Graves hyperthyroidism and a goiter of at least 48 mL. Diagnosis required suppressed TSH, elevated thyroid hormone, high 24-hour radioiodine uptake, and detectable TSH-receptor antibody.
Excluded: prior iodine-131 or thyroidectomy, moderate or severe ophthalmopathy, severe heart disease, a debilitating condition, and a goiter larger than 150 mL or causing compression.

schema.label: Design
