schema.text: Plasma hepatocyte growth factor study within a clinical trial of hypofractionated proton radiotherapy for unresectable liver cancer. The paper reports a median dose of 58.0 Gy and a median tumor size of 5.7 cm. It does not restate the protocol fraction number.

NCT00976898.schema_source: Hong et al., NPJ Precision Oncology 2018 (PMID 30374460). The full text was read. This is a plasma biomarker study within the proton trial. Fractionation is not restated.

specimens.window: Before proton radiotherapy
specimens.note: Liver dysfunction is a Child-Turcotte-Pugh score increase of at least 1 point within 3 months.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: The paper identifies this NCT as the phase 2 trial of total neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX followed by individualized chemoradiotherapy for borderline resectable pancreatic adenocarcinoma. Drug and radiation doses are not restated here. Losartan was not part of this trial.

NCT01591733.schema_source: Boucher et al., Clinical cancer research : an official journal of the American Association for Cancer Research 2023 (PMID 36749873). The full text was read. This correlative paper also analyzes a separate losartan trial. Doses for this trial are not restated.

specimens.window: Day 1, day 8, the start of FOLFIRINOX cycles 3, 4, 7, and 8, and after chemoradiotherapy
specimens.note: Cytokines. Surgical tissue was used for immunofluorescence.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-arm phase 2 trial of neoadjuvant trastuzumab, pertuzumab, and paclitaxel for 16 weeks in newly diagnosed HER2-positive inflammatory breast cancer. Milligram doses are in the protocol supplement and are not restated in the main text read here. Paclitaxel is added after the first dose of trastuzumab and pertuzumab.

NCT01796197.schema_source: Pernas et al., Therapeutic Advances in Medical Oncology 2022 (PMID 35923923). The full text was read.

specimens.window: Pretreatment day 1 and day 8, after one dose of trastuzumab and pertuzumab and before paclitaxel
specimens.note: RNA sequencing.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-institution nonrandomized phase 2 trial of intensity-modulated radiotherapy with or without concurrent doxorubicin for gross residual or unresectable non-anaplastic differentiated thyroid cancer. Primary endpoint is 2-year locoregional progression-free survival.

schema.label: Radiotherapy
schema.text: Supine, five-point mask. GTV is gross disease on CT, PET, and/or MRI and examination. CTV includes the GTV, thyroid bed, tracheoesophageal groove, and level VI and upper mediastinal nodes. PTV expands GTV and CTV by 3 to 5 mm. Planned doses are 70 Gy in 33 to 35 fractions to gross disease, 66 Gy in 33 fractions to close or positive margins, 60 Gy in 30 to 33 fractions to the operative or tumor bed, and 54 Gy in 30 fractions to low-risk central neck nodes. The lateral neck is not routine unless gross disease is present.

schema.label: Doxorubicin
schema.text: The first 8 patients received radiotherapy alone. From July 2014, weekly doxorubicin 10 mg/m2 was required during radiotherapy.

schema.label: Constraints
schema.text: Larynx maximum point dose under 70 Gy and mean under 45 Gy. Esophagus mean under 34 Gy. Lung mean under 21 Gy and V20 under 37 percent. Brachial plexus maximum under 65 Gy. Brainstem, optic nerves, and chiasm maximum under 54 Gy. Cord maximum under 45 Gy. Oral cavity mean under 40 Gy. Parotid mean under 26 Gy.

NCT01882816.schema_source: Romesser et al., Cancer 2021 (PMID 34293201). The full text was read.
eligibility: Gross residual or unresectable non-anaplastic differentiated thyroid carcinoma. A numeric laboratory and performance list was not in the sections read.

during.note: Acute events are during treatment and within 90 days after the last radiotherapy dose.

followup.item: Clinic visit
followup.window: Every 3 months for 2 years, every 6 months for the next 3 years, then annually
followup.note: Late toxicity is recorded from 90 days after the last dose.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-center double-blind placebo-controlled randomized trial. Twelve participants per arm.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Computer-generated assignment, concealed by the research pharmacy. Twice-daily oral delayed ileocolonic-release conjugated bile acids, 500 mg, or placebo, for 28 days, in adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes.

NCT02871882.schema_source: Calderon et al., EBioMedicine 2020 (PMID 32344198). The full text was read.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-arm open-label phase 2 trial of pembrolizumab for brain metastases of any solid-tumor histology. Cohort A is untreated brain metastases. Cohort B is recurrent progressive brain metastases. Primary endpoint is intracranial benefit.

schema.label: Treatment
schema.text: Pembrolizumab 200 mg intravenously every 3 weeks until progression, death, or unacceptable toxicity. No dose reductions. Interruptions up to 12 weeks are allowed. Concurrent radiation or other systemic therapy is not allowed, except aromatase or hormone inhibition or ovarian suppression.

NCT02886585.schema_source: Brastianos et al., Nature medicine 2023 (PMID 37268724). The full text was read.
eligibility: Age 18 or older. ECOG 2 or lower. Histologically confirmed metastatic solid tumor with at least one brain metastasis measuring at least 5 mm. Dexamethasone must be stable at 2 mg or less for at least 7 days.

Cohort A requires at least one previously untreated brain metastasis. Treatment-naive HER2-positive breast cancer, small-cell lung cancer, and oncogene-addicted non-small cell lung cancer are excluded when a first-line therapy has an overall-survival benefit.

Cohort B requires progressive brain metastases. Prior surgery, radiation, and central-nervous-system systemic therapy are allowed. Progression of a previously irradiated lesion must be unequivocal. Chemotherapy, targeted therapy, immunotherapy, or radiotherapy within 2 weeks is excluded.
Excluded: leptomeningeal disease and prior anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, or anti-PD-L2 therapy.

followup.item: Brain MRI and body CT
followup.window: Every 8 weeks
followup.note: Central review uses RANO for the brain and RECIST 1.1 outside the brain.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Multicenter open-label single-arm phase 2 trial of nivolumab plus radiosurgery for brain metastases from non-small cell lung cancer or renal cell carcinoma. Primary endpoint is intracranial progression-free survival.

schema.label: Treatment
schema.text: Nivolumab 240 mg or 480 mg intravenously, continued up to 2 years every 2 or 4 weeks until progression or unacceptable toxicity. Radiosurgery to all visible unirradiated brain lesions within 14 days after the first dose. Suggested single-fraction doses are 15 to 20 Gy under 2 cm, 15 to 18 Gy for 2 to 3 cm, and 15 Gy for 3 to 4 cm. PTV margin is 0 mm. If the planning MRI shows more disease, radiosurgery may still be given if the intracranial volume does not exceed 15 cc.

NCT02978404.schema_source: Wong et al., Neuro-Oncology Advances 2023 (PMID 37025758). The full text was read.
eligibility: Adults 18 or older with non-small cell lung cancer or renal cell carcinoma. Unirradiated brain metastases totaling 10 cc or less. No prior whole-brain radiotherapy and no prior immunotherapy. ECOG 0 or 1. Fewer than 4 prior lines of systemic therapy. Adequate blood, kidney, and liver function, without numeric cutoffs in the sections read. Able to complete questionnaires without assistance.

Excluded: pregnancy or nursing, a brainstem metastasis, seizure within 7 days of registration unless corticosteroids are used, inability to have MRI, and a systemic corticosteroid requirement above 10 mg prednisone equivalent.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-arm phase 2 trial of tocilizumab added to cyclosporine and mycophenolate mofetil after double-unit cord-blood transplantation.

schema.label: Conditioning
schema.text: Cyclophosphamide 50 mg/kg on day -6. Fludarabine 30 mg/m2 daily on days -6 to -2. Thiotepa 5 mg/kg daily on days -5 and -4. Total-body irradiation 200 cGy daily on days -2 and -1, 400 cGy total.

schema.label: Prophylaxis
schema.text: Intravenous cyclosporine and mycophenolate mofetil 15 mg/kg every 8 hours, capped at 1.5 g per dose, from day -3. Tocilizumab 8 mg/kg, capped at 800 mg, once on day -1.

NCT03434730.schema_source: Politikos et al., Blood Advances 2024 (PMID 40423982). The full text was read.
eligibility: Age 18 to 65 with no suitable matched related or unrelated donor in the needed time. Eligible diseases include AML in morphologic remission or with at most 10 percent blasts, ALL or mixed-phenotype leukemia in morphologic remission, MDS or a myeloproliferative neoplasm with at most 10 percent blasts, aggressive lymphoma in metabolic complete remission, and indolent lymphoma with at least stable disease.

Karnofsky score at least 70. GFR at least 60 mL/min/1.73 m2. Bilirubin under 1.5 mg/dL. ALT at most 3 times the upper limit of normal. DLCO at least 50 percent predicted. Left-ventricular ejection fraction above 50 percent. Albumin at least 3.0 g/dL. Age-adjusted HCT comorbidity index 7 or lower.
Excluded: myelofibrosis, a previous allograft, HIV or HTLV-1, and active infection.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Investigator-initiated trial for oligometastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer. This paper studies screening and imaging review. It states the treatment but not the stereotactic dose.

schema.label: Treatment
schema.text: Androgen deprivation for 9 months, stereotactic ablative radiotherapy to all metastatic sites, and radium-223 55 kBq/kg intravenously every 4 weeks for 6 doses.

NCT03361735.schema_source: Dorff et al., Journal of Clinical Medicine 2023 (PMID 36902798). The full text was read. This paper studies screening and imaging review and states the systemic and radiopharmaceutical doses, not the stereotactic dose.
eligibility: Men with oligometastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer. At least one bone metastasis and no more than five metastatic sites, including soft tissue.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-arm phase 2 trial, SATURN, for oligorecurrent metastatic prostate cancer after radical prostatectomy. Primary endpoint is the percentage with PSA under 0.05 ng/mL 6 months after testosterone recovery to at least 150 ng/dL.

schema.label: Treatment
schema.text: Six months of androgen annihilation therapy: leuprolide, abiraterone acetate plus prednisone, and apalutamide, plus metastasis-directed stereotactic body radiotherapy. The stereotactic dose and fractionation were not in the sections read.

NCT03902951.schema_source: Nikitas et al., European urology 2024 (PMID 38494380). The full text was read.
eligibility: One to five nonvisceral, extrapelvic metastases on PSMA PET/CT after prior radical prostatectomy. A fuller eligibility list was not in the sections read.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-arm phase 2 protocol of pembrolizumab with cisplatin and radiation for unresectable, incompletely resected, recurrent, or metastatic vulvar squamous carcinoma.

schema.label: Safety cohort
schema.text: The first 3 patients treated with definitive chemoradiation receive pembrolizumab on cycle 1, then resume at cycle 4 after chemoradiation, for 10 cycles total.

schema.label: Other patients
schema.text: Weekly cisplatin and pembrolizumab every 3 weeks during daily radiation, then pembrolizumab maintenance for 12 cycles. The procedures section prescribes pembrolizumab 200 mg as a 30-minute infusion. The rationale section prints the same schedule as 200 mg/m2. Cisplatin is 40 mg/m2 over 30 to 60 minutes weekly, and may be given up to day 3. Pembrolizumab is given before cisplatin.

schema.label: Radiation
schema.text: For locally advanced or unresectable disease, external-beam radiotherapy covers the vulva and regional nodes, including inguinofemoral and external and internal iliac regions as indicated by the primary site. Treatment follows standard of care. Patients who cannot safely receive at least 30 Gy in 10 fractions are not eligible. A single prescribed curative dose beyond that minimum is not stated.

NCT04430699.schema_source: Yeku et al., Journal of Translational Medicine 2020 (PMID 32928237). The full text was read.
eligibility: Women 18 or older with histologically or cytologically confirmed unresectable, incompletely resected, recurrent, or metastatic vulvar squamous carcinoma. Unresectable disease includes T2 or T3 primary tumors, N0 to 3, M0, not amenable to radical vulvectomy.
Prior chemotherapy, immunotherapy, or radiation is allowed. Reirradiation of a previously treated site is not. Recurrent disease may not have had more than two prior lines of cytotoxic therapy.

pretreatment.item: Imaging and tissue markers
pretreatment.note: Imaging is repeated every 3 cycles of 21 days. HPV, PD-L1, and microsatellite status are collected and are not eligibility criteria.

during.note: CTCAE version 5.0.

followup.item: Survival
followup.window: Up to 3 years or until death
followup.note: Survival is checked every 6 months.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Randomized phase 2 trial of preoperative chemoradiation and surgery with or without induction chemotherapy for esophageal cancer. This paper is a secondary PET analysis and restates the regimen.

schema.label: No induction
schema.text: 50.4 Gy in 28 fractions with intensity-modulated protons or photons. Concurrent fluorouracil 250 mg/m2 per day as a 24-hour infusion Monday through Friday for 5 weeks, and oxaliplatin 40 mg/m2 intravenously once a week for 5 weeks.

schema.label: Induction
schema.text: Up to two 4-week cycles: fluorouracil 2200 mg/m2 over 48 hours starting on days 1 and 15, and oxaliplatin 100 mg/m2 on days 1 and 15. PET or endoscopy after the first cycle. If there is no progression or adverse event, a second cycle is given, then the same chemoradiation as the no-induction arm.

NCT00525915.schema_source: Harada et al., Targeted oncology 2018 (PMID 29218623). The full text was read. This is a secondary PET analysis that restates the trial regimen.
eligibility: Younger than 76 years. ECOG 0 or 1. Adequate organ function, without numeric cutoffs in the sections read. Clinical stage T1 node-positive, or T2 or T3 with any nodal status. Eligible for trimodality therapy.

pretreatment.item: FDG-PET
pretreatment.window: Baseline, after one cycle of induction chemotherapy, and 5 to 7 weeks after chemoradiation
pretreatment.note: A PET response in this analysis is at least a 35 percent reduction in SUV.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-center prospective study, SMC NB-2009, replacing total-body irradiation with iodine-131 MIBG in tandem high-dose chemotherapy and autologous transplantation for high-risk neuroblastoma.

schema.label: Induction
schema.text: Nine alternating cycles of CEDC and ICE at 4-week intervals. CEDC: cisplatin 60 mg/m2 on day 0, etoposide 100 mg/m2 on days 2 and 5, doxorubicin 30 mg/m2 on day 2, and cyclophosphamide 30 mg/kg on days 3 and 4. ICE: the table prints ifosfamide as 1 200 mg/m2/day on days 0 to 4, carboplatin 400 mg/m2 on days 0 and 1, and etoposide 100 mg/m2 on days 0 to 4. Doses are reduced by age under 24 months. Surgery is usually after six cycles. Stem cells are collected after cycle 7.

schema.label: Tandem transplant
schema.text: First regimen, CEC: carboplatin, etoposide, and cyclophosphamide, each as printed in the chemotherapy table, on days -7 to -2. Second regimen for metastatic MIBG-avid tumors: iodine-131 MIBG 18 or 12 mCi/kg on day -21, then thiotepa 200 mg/m2 on days -6 to -4 and melphalan 60 mg/m2 on days -3 and -2. Localized or nonavid tumors omit MIBG and use thiotepa 300 mg/m2 on days -6 to -4 with the same melphalan.

schema.label: After transplant
schema.text: Local radiotherapy to the primary site about 6 weeks after the second transplant: 15 Gy at 1.5 Gy for a complete resection, or 21.6 Gy or 30.6 Gy at 1.8 Gy for an incomplete resection, according to residual MIBG or PET uptake. Metastatic sites are not irradiated. Starting about 9 weeks after the second transplant, 13-cis-retinoic acid 125 mg/m2/day for 14 days every 4 weeks and interleukin-2 2 million U/m2/day subcutaneously for 5 days every 4 weeks, until 1 year after the second transplant.

NCT03061656.schema_source: Lee et al., Journal of Hematology & Oncology 2017 (PMID 28511709). The full text was read.
eligibility: Newly diagnosed high-risk neuroblastoma. Older than 1 year with INSS stage 4, or MYCN amplification at any stage. MYCN amplification is more than four times the control-probe signal.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-institution single-arm phase 2 trial of sorafenib followed by yttrium-90 glass microspheres for advanced or metastatic hepatocellular carcinoma. The primary endpoint began as safety in the first 10 patients and was amended to progression-free survival, with accrual extended toward 40 patients.

schema.label: Treatment
schema.text: Sorafenib starts at 400 mg twice daily, 4 weeks plus or minus 1 week before radioembolization. Technetium-99m macroaggregated albumin mapping is done within 1 week of enrollment. Yttrium-90 glass microspheres (TheraSphere) are given at a later visit. The paper does not state a protocol activity or absorbed-dose prescription. Restaging CT is at week 16, using RECIST 1.1.

NCT01900002.schema_source: Kaseb et al., Journal of Hepatocellular Carcinoma 2021 (PMID 34527608). The full text was read.
eligibility: Older than 18 years. ECOG 0 or 1. Child-Pugh A. Histologic, cytologic, or AASLD clinical diagnosis of advanced or metastatic hepatocellular carcinoma. The remainder of the inclusion paragraph was not fully captured beyond those criteria.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-center single-arm phase 2 trial, Simon two-stage, of neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX then gemcitabine chemoradiation for borderline-resectable pancreatic adenocarcinoma. Primary endpoint is R0 resection among patients who receive at least one cycle. The trial stopped early for slow accrual.

schema.label: Induction
schema.text: FOLFIRINOX every 2 weeks for 4 cycles: oxaliplatin 85 mg/m2, leucovorin 400 mg/m2, irinotecan 180 mg/m2, fluorouracil 400 mg/m2 bolus, then fluorouracil 2400 mg/m2 over 46 hours. CT after 4 cycles. Progression leaves the chemoradiation phase.

schema.label: Chemoradiation
schema.text: Starts within 6 weeks after induction. IMRT, 50.4 Gy in 28 fractions, with weekly gemcitabine 400 mg/m2. Four-dimensional simulation. Elective nodal irradiation is not used. Organ constraints are in a supplement and are not restated here. Imaging 4 to 6 weeks after treatment. Resection if the disease is then resectable.

NCT01897454.schema_source: Acuna-Villaorduna et al., Cancer Control : Journal of the Moffitt Cancer Center 2022 (PMID 36221952). The full text was read.
eligibility: Adults with treatment-naive, histologically confirmed pancreatic adenocarcinoma called borderline resectable by a multidisciplinary team using the Callery consensus. ECOG 0 or 1. Life expectancy greater than 6 months.

Leukocytes at least 3000/microliter, neutrophils at least 1500/microliter, platelets at least 100,000/microliter, total bilirubin at most 2 mg/dL, AST and ALT at most 2.5 times the upper limit, and creatinine within normal limits.
Excluded: uncontrolled intercurrent illness, HIV, pregnancy, and another active malignancy except non-melanoma skin cancer or cervical carcinoma in situ.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-center single-arm phase 2 trial of postoperative radiotherapy to an extensive clinical target volume for locally advanced thoracic esophageal squamous cell carcinoma. Primary endpoint is 2-year local control. Local control means no recurrence at the stump or in nodes inside the field.

schema.label: Radiotherapy
schema.text: Starts within 3 months after surgery. 6 MV photons, IMRT, 40 Gy in 20 fractions, 2 Gy per day, 5 days per week. CTV includes the tumor bed when preoperative CT is available, the anastomosis, bilateral supraclavicular nodes, all mediastinal nodal stations, and left gastric and celiac nodes. PTV adds 1 cm. The field beside the cord may be adjusted. No concurrent chemotherapy is described.

NCT02384811.schema_source: Zhang et al., Frontiers in Oncology 2021 (PMID 34295813). The full text was read.
eligibility: Radical transthoracic resection with negative margins within 3 months. Histologically confirmed esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, pT3 to 4 or node-positive, M0, AJCC 7th edition.

schema.label: Radiotherapy
schema.text: The paper states that definitive chemoradiotherapy on these protocols used IMRT, 60 to 68 Gy to the PTV of the GTV in 16 to 23 daily fractions. Four-dimensional simulation. GTV is the visible primary tumor and positive nodes on all breathing phases. PTV expands the GTV by 5 to 6 mm. Involved-node irradiation is used.

schema.label: Chemotherapy
schema.text: Weekly concurrent docetaxel or paclitaxel plus platinum. The cohort description gives weekly docetaxel 25 mg/m2 and platinum 25 mg/m2 for 3 to 5 cycles, depending on the number of fractions. No consolidation or adjuvant therapy after chemoradiotherapy.

NCT02577341.schema_source: Liu et al., Frontiers in Oncology 2022 (PMID 36465342). The full text was read. The analyzed cohort also includes NCT02573506 and patients treated according to those protocols.
eligibility: The analyzed patients, including this trial, had biopsy-proven non-small cell lung cancer, stage IIIA to IIIC by AJCC 8th edition, curative concurrent chemoradiotherapy, no adjuvant or consolidation therapy, age 18 or older, and ECOG 0 to 2. Metastatic disease at diagnosis was excluded.

during.window: Before chemoradiotherapy, weekly during it, and monthly for 12 months after it
during.note: Lymphocyte counts. Lymphopenia is graded with CTCAE version 5.0.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Multicenter prospective phase 2 study of adjuvant radiotherapy after radical cystectomy for muscle-invasive bladder cancer. Planned accrual is 76. Radiotherapy starts in weeks 6 to 12 after cystectomy. Primary endpoint is acute grade 3 or higher intestinal toxicity, or grade 4 urinary toxicity after neobladder reconstruction, within 12 weeks.

schema.label: Dose
schema.text: VMAT, 50 Gy in 25 fractions to pelvic nodes, and to the bladder bed only if the surgical margin is positive. Nodes along the common, internal, and external iliac arteries, obturator fossa, and presacral nodes are included. CTV expands the nodal volume by 2 mm and PTV adds 5 mm. A simultaneous boost is prescribed up to 70 Gy to PET-avid nodes. The paper equates that boost with a normalized dose of 74 Gy in 2 Gy fractions using an alpha/beta of 10. The abstract's 74 Gy figure is that equivalent dose. Daily cone-beam CT. 6 to 18 MV photons.

NCT02397434.schema_source: Fonteyne et al., BMC Cancer 2017 (PMID 28464906). The full text was read.
eligibility: M0 muscle-invasive bladder cancer after cystectomy and extended pelvic node dissection, with at least one of: pT3 with lymphovascular invasion, pT4, fewer than 10 nodes removed, positive nodes, or a positive margin.
WHO performance status 0 to 2. Age 18 or older.

Excluded: distant metastasis, prior pelvic irradiation, a condition that would prevent compliance, and another primary tumor except an incidentally removed prostate cancer, non-melanoma skin cancer, or a tumor diagnosed at least 5 years earlier.

pretreatment.item: FDG PET-CT
pretreatment.window: Recommended, not required, 4 to 10 weeks after cystectomy
pretreatment.note: To look for distant metastases. Suspicious nodes may still be included and boosted.

pretreatment.item: Planning CT
pretreatment.note: Supine, 3 mm slices from the lung apex to mid-femur.

followup.item: Clinic and blood tests
followup.window: 1 month after radiotherapy, then every 3 months
followup.note: Sedimentation rate, blood count with differential, creatinine, electrolytes, liver tests, and alkaline phosphatase.

followup.item: CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis
followup.window: Every 3 to 6 months in year 1 if asymptomatic, then every 6 months to 5 years, then yearly
followup.note: Until progression.

specimens.window: Day 1 and the last day of radiotherapy
specimens.note: Biomarker evaluation.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Multicenter non-randomized phase 2 trial in resectable HPV-unrelated head and neck squamous carcinoma. Group 1, reported here, receives one neoadjuvant dose of pembrolizumab, then surgery. High-risk pathology (positive margin and/or extranodal extension) is scheduled for postoperative chemoradiation and then adjuvant pembrolizumab. Low or intermediate risk is scheduled for postoperative radiotherapy or observation, without adjuvant pembrolizumab. Physician discretion can still give chemoradiation for intermediate-risk pathology.

schema.label: Pembrolizumab
schema.text: 200 mg intravenously once, 13 to 22 days before surgery. After high-risk chemoradiation, adverse events must be grade 1 or lower and at least 3 months must have passed from surgery before adjuvant pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks for six doses.

schema.label: Group 2
schema.text: Two neoadjuvant doses, then surgery, then postoperative chemoradiation if high risk or radiotherapy or observation if not. No adjuvant pembrolizumab. Not reported in this paper.

NCT02296684.schema_source: Uppaluri et al., Clinical cancer research : an official journal of the American Association for Cancer Research 2020 (PMID 32665297). The full text was read.
eligibility: Resectable clinical stage III to IVb, AJCC 7th edition, HPV-unrelated squamous carcinoma of the oral cavity, larynx, hypopharynx, or p16-negative oropharynx. Measurable disease by RECIST 1.1. ECOG 0 or 1.

Neutrophils at least 1,500/mcL, platelets at least 100,000/mcL, hemoglobin at least 9 g/dL, total bilirubin at most 1.5 times the upper limit, AST and ALT at most 2.5 times the upper limit, and creatinine at most 1.5 times the upper limit or clearance at least 30 mL/min.
Excluded: HPV-related oropharynx cancer, active autoimmune disease, and immunodeficiency.

pretreatment.item: Eligibility tests
pretreatment.note: Complete blood count, metabolic panel, pregnancy test when applicable, coagulation and thyroid panels, urinalysis, and CT of the neck and chest.

pretreatment.item: Baseline tumor assessment
pretreatment.note: Physical examination, neck CT, biopsy of the primary tumor, and peripheral blood.

during.window: The day before or the day of surgery
during.note: After patient 20, neck CT within 10 days before surgery was added.
CTCAE version 4.0 and Clavien-Dindo surgical complications. Tumor and blood are collected on the day of surgery.

specimens.window: Before pembrolizumab and on the day of surgery
specimens.note: Correlative studies.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-institution phase 2 trial of pharmacological ascorbate with radiation and temozolomide for newly diagnosed glioblastoma, including IDH-mutant grade 4 astrocytoma.

schema.label: Concomitant phase
schema.text: Radiation 61.2 Gy in 34 fractions and temozolomide 75 mg/m2 daily for a maximum of 49 days. Ascorbate 87.5 g intravenously three times weekly, at a maximum rate of 500 mL per hour, from day 1 of radiation until the first day of adjuvant cycle 1.

schema.label: Adjuvant phase
schema.text: Temozolomide 150 mg/m2 on days 1 to 5 of a 28-day cycle, with one escalation to 200 mg/m2 in cycle 2 if tolerated, through cycle 6 or progression. Ascorbate 87.5 g twice weekly. Tumor-treating fields are prohibited during protocol therapy and allowed afterward.

NCT02344355.schema_source: Petronek et al., Clinical cancer research : an official journal of the American Association for Cancer Research 2024 (PMID 37773633). The full text was read.
eligibility: Newly diagnosed glioblastoma, including IDH-mutant grade 4 astrocytoma. After consent, glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency is checked and a 15 g ascorbate test infusion is given. A fuller performance and laboratory list was not in the sections read.

pretreatment.item: Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase test and ascorbate test dose
pretreatment.note: 15 g ascorbate infusion.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Allogeneic bone marrow transplant with post-transplant cyclophosphamide for severe recessive dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa, with mesenchymal stromal cell infusions. Drug milligram doses and the original total-body irradiation prescription are in the supplement and are not restated in the main text.

schema.label: Conditioning
schema.text: Rabbit anti-thymocyte globulin, cyclophosphamide, fludarabine, and low-dose total-body irradiation. After graft failure in early patients, total-body irradiation was increased from 300 cGy to 400 cGy. Graft-versus-host prophylaxis is post-transplant cyclophosphamide and mycophenolate mofetil, with or without tacrolimus.

NCT02582775.schema_source: Ebens et al., The British journal of dermatology 2019 (PMID 30843184). The full text was read.
eligibility: Recessive dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa confirmed by COL7A1 mutation, reduced or absent type VII collagen immunofluorescence, and absent normal anchoring structures on immunoelectron microscopy, with generalized severe disease. An external panel reviewed whether the severity justified transplant.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-arm phase 2 cohort of postoperative intensity-modulated radiotherapy plus docetaxel and nedaplatin for high-risk salivary gland carcinoma that is not adenoid cystic carcinoma. Primary endpoint is 5-year disease-free survival. A retrospective radiotherapy-alone cohort in the same paper is not this trial.

schema.label: Radiotherapy
schema.text: IMRT in a thermoplastic head, neck, and shoulder mask. CTV1 is residual tumor and/or the tumor bed. CTV2 adds typical pathways and high-risk nodes. CTV3 is low-risk nodes. PTV expands CTV1 by 5 mm and CTV2 and CTV3 by 3 mm. Doses are 66 to 70 Gy, 60 Gy, and 54 Gy in 30 to 32 fractions.

schema.label: Chemotherapy
schema.text: Two cycles every 3 weeks from day 1: docetaxel 70 mg/m2 on day 1 and nedaplatin 35 mg/m2 on days 1 and 2. Dexamethasone 8 mg orally twice daily for 3 days before chemotherapy. Chemotherapy requires adequate marrow, liver, and kidney function and is stopped if delayed more than 2 weeks.

NCT02776163.schema_source: Dou et al., Cancer Medicine 2026 (PMID 41878954). The full text was read.
eligibility: Age 18 to 75. After resection: T1 to 2 with N1 to 3, or T3 to 4 with N0 to 3, AJCC 7th edition. Grade III salivary gland carcinoma, or grade II with R2 resection or N1 to 3. Karnofsky score 70 or higher. No distant metastasis. Expected survival at least 6 months.

Histologies include salivary duct carcinoma, grade 2 to 3 carcinoma ex pleomorphic adenoma, grade 2 to 3 mucoepidermoid carcinoma, grade 3 adenocarcinoma NOS, and other grade 2 to 3 histologies. Lymphoepithelial carcinoma, carcinosarcoma, and neuroendocrine carcinoma are excluded. Biopsy only, another malignancy within 5 years except nonmelanoma skin cancer, and significant medical illness are excluded.

pretreatment.item: History, examination, blood count, chemistry, and imaging
pretreatment.note: Contrast MRI or CT of the head and neck, plus other staging as indicated. Residual disease is reviewed by a multidisciplinary team.

during.note: Toxicity uses CTCAE version 4.03.

followup.item: Clinic visit
followup.window: Every 3 months for 2 years after radiotherapy, then every 6 months from the third year
followup.note: The sentence in the extract ends at that point.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-arm, single-center phase 2 feasibility trial of definitive radiotherapy to defer systemic therapy for oligometastatic renal cell carcinoma. Co-primary endpoints are feasibility, defined as completing all planned radiotherapy with fewer than 7 days of unplanned breaks, and progression-free survival. A later second cohort is not reported in this paper.

schema.label: Radiotherapy
schema.text: All sites are treated and systemic therapy is held. Stereotactic body radiotherapy is 5 or fewer fractions of at least 7 Gy. If that is unsafe, hypofractionated intensity-modulated radiotherapy is 60 to 70 Gy in 10 fractions or 52.5 to 67.5 Gy in 15 fractions. Further radiotherapy is allowed for later progression in three or fewer lesions. Lung or upper-abdominal non-skeletal tumors use four-dimensional CT. Breath-hold gating is used if motion exceeds 1 cm. Daily cone-beam CT or CT-on-rails is generally used.

NCT03575611.schema_source: Tang et al., The Lancet. Oncology 2021 (PMID 34717797). The full text was read.
eligibility: Age 18 or older. Histologically confirmed renal cell carcinoma with up to five metastatic sites, any histology. ECOG 0 to 2. A candidate for definitive radiotherapy to all sites.
No prior systemic therapy for metastatic disease, or only one prior systemic therapy stopped at least 1 month before enrolment.

Neutrophils at least 1000 per microliter, platelets at least 50,000 per microliter, hemoglobin at least 9 g/dL. AST and ALT at most 3 times the upper limit of normal, or 5 times if liver metastases are present. The printed bilirubin limit is 11.5 mg/dL and is not restated as a corrected value. A negative pregnancy test is required when applicable.

Excluded: pregnancy, comorbidities that make radiotherapy unsafe (the paper gives active scleroderma or other rheumatologic disease as examples), known psychiatric or substance-use disorders, and diffuse disease such as malignant effusion, leptomeningeal disease, diffuse marrow involvement, or peritoneal carcinomatosis.

pretreatment.item: Staging
pretreatment.note: CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis, PET, and MRI of the abdomen. IMDC risk is recorded.

pretreatment.item: Metastatic biopsy
pretreatment.note: Biopsy of a metastatic lesion.

followup.item: Restaging, blood count, and adverse events
followup.window: Every 12 weeks in year 1, then every 18 weeks in year 2
followup.note: CTCAE version 4.0. Imaging is contrast CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis, or chest CT plus MRI of the abdomen and pelvis if renal function is insufficient. Central review of progression. Protocol follow-up continues until death or start of systemic therapy.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-arm phase 2 trial of toripalimab plus intensity-modulated radiotherapy for unresectable locally recurrent nasopharyngeal carcinoma. Primary endpoint is objective response 3 months after radiotherapy.

schema.label: Treatment
schema.text: Toripalimab 240 mg intravenously every 3 weeks for a maximum of seven cycles. No dose modification. Radiotherapy starts after the first cycle. Prescribed doses are 60 Gy, 60 Gy, and 54 Gy in 27 fractions to the planning volumes from the primary tumor, gross neck nodes, and clinical target volume. Clinical target volume is the primary tumor plus a 0.5 to 1.0 cm margin. Further planning details are in a supplement and are not restated here.

NCT03854838.schema_source: Hua et al., Journal for Immunotherapy of Cancer 2021 (PMID 34782428). The full text was read.
eligibility: Age 18 to 65. Histologically confirmed nasopharyngeal carcinoma with local recurrence, recurrent stage II to IVa, unsuitable for local surgery. More than 12 months from the end of prior radiotherapy. No systemic chemotherapy yet for the recurrence. ECOG 0 or 1. At least one measurable lesion by RECIST 1.1. Adequate organ function, without numeric cutoffs in the sections read.

Excluded: active autoimmune disease, immunosuppressive medication, active hepatitis B or C, uncontrolled hypertension or cardiac disease, prior anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-L1 therapy, and pregnancy or breastfeeding.

pretreatment.item: History, examination, and blood tests
pretreatment.note: Hematologic and biochemical analyses and nasopharyngoscopy.

pretreatment.item: Imaging
pretreatment.note: MRI, or contrast CT if MRI is contraindicated, of the head and neck. FDG-PET to exclude distant metastasis.

followup.item: Efficacy and safety visits
followup.window: Every 3 months after radiotherapy until death
followup.note: Nasopharyngoscopy and MRI for response. Adverse events use CTCAE version 5.0 and RTOG acute and late scores. Acute events are during radiotherapy or within 3 months. Late events are after 3 months.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Bayesian phase 2 platform, PIONEER-Panc, for localized pancreatic adenocarcinoma. Six cohorts are defined by resectable, borderline, or locally advanced stage, and by treatment-naive or previously treated status. Each cohort has a control arm and may have experimental arms. Randomization is adaptive.

schema.label: Control treatment
schema.text: For treatment-naive patients the control systemic therapy is modified FOLFIRINOX. Previously treated patients may have received gemcitabine, gemcitabine with cisplatin, gemcitabine with nab-paclitaxel, gemcitabine with capecitabine, or FOLFIRINOX. Radiation in a control arm is standard for borderline disease and optional for resectable disease. Techniques may include stereotactic body radiotherapy, hypofractionated radiotherapy, or standard fractionation with concurrent chemotherapy. A single Gray prescription is not stated.

NCT04481204.schema_source: Douglas et al., BMC Cancer 2022 (PMID 34980020). The full text was read.
eligibility: Localized pancreatic adenocarcinoma placed in one of the six stage and treatment-history cohorts. The detailed criterion figure was not transcribed into narrative cutoffs.

during.note: Systemic therapy visits are generally every 1 to 3 months.

followup.item: Post-radiation follow-up
followup.window: Every 1 to 6 months

specimens.item: Biopsy or tissue and serial blood
specimens.window: Before and after treatment when feasible
specimens.note: Liquid biopsy, radiomics, and quality-of-life questionnaires.

submission.label: Randomization website
submission.text: Randomization uses the MD Anderson Clinical Trial Conduct website.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Two-center single-arm phase 2 trial of consolidative stereotactic radiotherapy for oligo-residual EGFR-mutant metastatic non-small cell lung cancer after a first-line third-generation EGFR inhibitor. The inhibitor is not held. Primary endpoint is progression-free survival from the start of the inhibitor.

schema.label: Radiotherapy
schema.text: All residual disease is treated. Cranial stereotactic radiotherapy is mainly 27 Gy in 3 fractions. Extracranial dose and fractionation follow NRG-BR001 and are listed in a supplement, not restated here. Dose choice is otherwise at the treating radiation oncologist's discretion.

NCT04764214.schema_source: Zhou et al., eClinicalMedicine 2024 (PMID 39398493). The full text was read.
eligibility: Age 18 to 75. ECOG 0 to 2. Pathologically confirmed stage IV non-small cell lung cancer, AJCC 8th edition, with EGFR exon 19 deletion or exon 21 L858R. At least one measurable lesion by RECIST 1.1. Oligo-residual disease after a third-generation EGFR inhibitor that the investigator considers suitable for consolidative stereotactic radiotherapy.

Oligo-residual disease may be cranial, extracranial, or both. Without baseline brain metastases, or after an intracranial complete response, extracranial residual disease is limited to three organs and five lesions. A node with short diameter 1 cm or less and no malignant features is considered benign. Combined effusion or multiple pleural or peritoneal nodules are excluded. PET/CT confirms the oligo-residual state.
Excluded: another malignancy, pregnancy or breastfeeding, a condition that would prevent compliance or consent, and residual tumors not suitable for stereotactic radiotherapy.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-center single-arm phase 2 trial of consolidative stereotactic radiotherapy for oligo-residual metastatic non-small cell lung cancer without a sensitizing driver mutation, after first-line chemoimmunotherapy. Maintenance systemic therapy is not held. Primary endpoint is progression-free survival from the start of chemoimmunotherapy.

schema.label: Radiotherapy
schema.text: All residual lesions are treated. Cranial stereotactic radiotherapy is 27 Gy in 3 fractions. Extracranial regimens follow NRG-BR001 and are not restated here. Radiotherapy is scheduled between cycles of maintenance therapy. Maintenance immunotherapy continues during and after radiotherapy for up to 2 years, or until progression or intolerable toxicity.

NCT04767009.schema_source: Chen et al., PLOS Medicine 2025 (PMID 40748918). The full text was read.
eligibility: Age 18 to 75. ECOG 0 or 1. Pathologically confirmed stage IV non-small cell lung cancer, AJCC 8th edition, without a common sensitizing driver mutation. First-line treatment is a commercial PD-1 or PD-L1 inhibitor plus platinum doublet.

Eligibility is assessed after 4 cycles and then every 2 to 3 months for a year. PET/CT confirms oligo-residual disease. Extracranial residual disease, including the primary tumor, is limited to three organs and five lesions when there are no baseline brain metastases or the brain has had a complete response. Cranial oligo-residual disease is at most 10 brain metastases, each under 10 mL and under 3 cm, with cumulative volume 15 mL or less, and no extracranial progression.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: The paper states that a larger randomized trial of hypofractionated versus conventionally fractionated premastectomy radiotherapy has been started and gives this NCT. It does not state that trial's eligibility, doses, or schedule. The 40.05 Gy and 50 Gy schedules in the paper belong to the earlier trial, NCT02912312.

NCT05774678.schema_source: Schaverien et al., JAMA Network Open 2024 (PMID 38578640). The full text was read. The reported trial is NCT02912312. This NCT is named only as a subsequent trial.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Two-arm randomized phase III trial (ESOPEC, NCT02509286) comparing perioperative FLOT chemotherapy plus surgery with neoadjuvant CROSS chemoradiation plus surgery for esophageal adenocarcinoma. Primary endpoint is overall survival from the start of study treatment, with follow-up for at least 36 months or until death.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients are randomized to Arm A or Arm B. Surgery in both arms is preferably 4 to 6 weeks after neoadjuvant treatment. Open, minimally invasive, or hybrid resection is allowed.

arms.label: Arm A, FLOT
arms.text: Four preoperative and four postoperative 14-day cycles. Each cycle: 5-FU 2600 mg/m2 over 24 hours on day 1, leucovorin 200 mg/m2 over 2 hours on day 1, oxaliplatin 85 mg/m2 over 2 hours on day 1, and docetaxel 50 mg/m2 over 1 hour, every 2 weeks.

arms.label: Arm B, CROSS
arms.text: External-beam 3D conformal radiotherapy, 41.4 Gy in 23 fractions of 1.8 Gy, with weekly paclitaxel 50 mg/m2 and carboplatin AUC 2 on days 1, 8, 15, 22, and 29.

NCT02509286.schema_source: Open-access protocol, Hoeppner et al., BMC Cancer 2016 (PMID 27435280). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Histologically proven esophageal adenocarcinoma, cT1 N+ M0 or cT2-4a N0 or N+ M0. cT4a must be judged curatively resectable by the local surgeon before randomization.
Age at least 18 years, no prior abdominal or thoracic radiotherapy, ECOG 0 to 2, and written informed consent.

Adequate marrow (WBC above 3 x 10^9/L, hemoglobin above 9 g/dL, platelets above 100 x 10^9/L), GFR above 60 mL/min, and liver tests within the printed limits. Cardiac history requires ejection fraction above 50%.

Excluded: squamous, adenosquamous, or other non-adenocarcinoma histology; inoperable or metastatic disease; cT1N0 or cT4b; gastric carcinoma; prior chemotherapy for gastrointestinal cancer; significant active cardiac or lung disease (FEV1 below 1.5 L); peripheral neuropathy above grade 1; pregnancy or lactation; another interfering intervention trial.

pretreatment.item: Screening
pretreatment.note: Physical examination, history, demographics, vital signs, weight, ECG, standard laboratories, upper endoscopy with biopsies, endoscopic ultrasound, and CT of the thorax and abdomen. Cardiac or pulmonary testing is mandatory if there is a suggestive history or symptoms.

during.window: Every 2 weeks on FLOT and weekly during CROSS
during.note: Vital signs, weight, ECG, and standard and hematologic laboratories.

followup.item: Survival and clinical follow-up
followup.window: First visit at 6 months from the start of treatment, then every 3 months in year 1 and every 6 months from year 2
followup.note: Minimum follow-up is 3 years, or until death. Trial follow-up ends 3 years after the last patient's study treatment starts.

specimens.window: Before treatment and during treatment
specimens.note: Blood for circulating tumor cells, circulating tumor DNA, miRNA, adipokines, inflammatory markers, and proteomic studies. Pretreatment biopsies and operative FFPE specimens are centrally biobanked.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-institution, open-label, parallel-group randomized phase II pilot (Extrem-ion) of neoadjuvant hypofractionated ion radiotherapy for resectable extremity soft-tissue sarcoma. Adaptive two-stage design. Primary endpoint is the rate of wound healing disorders from the start of radiotherapy until at most 120 days after planned resection, or until treatment-related discontinuation.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Block randomization 1:1 with a web-based tool. Both arms receive 39 Gy (RBE) in 13 fractions, 5 to 6 fractions per week, prescribed to the PTV. No extremity organ has a specific dose constraint in the protocol.

arms.label: Arm A
arms.text: Proton therapy, raster-scan, 39 Gy (RBE) in 13 fractions.

arms.label: Arm B
arms.text: Carbon-ion therapy, raster-scan, 39 Gy (RBE) in 13 fractions.

NCT04946357.schema_source: Open-access protocol, Brugemann et al., BMC Cancer 2022 (PMID 35550036). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Histologically confirmed extremity soft-tissue sarcoma with an indication for perioperative radiotherapy, resectable or marginally resectable.
Karnofsky index at least 70%, age at least 18 years, and written informed consent.

Excluded: stage IV, lymph-node metastasis, metal implants that affect ion planning, prior radiotherapy in the treatment area, desmoid tumors, another trial that could influence results, and active medical implants without an ion-beam permit.

pretreatment.item: Planning imaging and incision mark
pretreatment.note: Planning CT with 3 mm slices in the treatment position and MRI, including a post-gadolinium T1 sequence. The surgeon marks the planned incision, shown on contrast CT by a steel wire so that region can be spared if possible.

during.window: Weekly during radiotherapy and at the end of treatment
during.note: Acute adverse events by CTCAE v5.0. MRI of the extremity is planned 3 weeks after radiotherapy, and resection 4 to 6 weeks after radiotherapy.

followup.item: Clinical and imaging follow-up
followup.window: 6 weeks after resection, then 3, 6, 9, and 12 months
followup.note: History, symptoms, and toxicity at each visit. Extremity MRI and chest CT are listed through 12 months. QLQ-C30 is scheduled before treatment, 3 weeks after radiotherapy, 6 months after surgery, and 12 months after surgery. Regular study end is 12 months after surgery.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Prospective multicenter randomized phase III trial (Hi-RISE, NCT04025164) after breast-conserving surgery. Protocol version 1.0 was approved in April 2018, with a later modification in January 2021. Planned enrollment is 2904. Follow-up is at least 5 years.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Stratified block randomization by age (at least 50 versus under 50), ER status, axillary lymph-node status, and adjuvant chemotherapy (yes versus no).

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Eligible patients are randomized 1:1. At least 95% of the PTV must receive 95% of the prescription. IMRT or VMAT is allowed.

arms.label: CFRTseq
arms.text: 50 Gy in 25 fractions over 5 weeks to the whole breast with or without regional nodes, then a sequential tumor-bed boost of 10 Gy in 5 fractions.

arms.label: HFRTsib
arms.text: 40 Gy in 15 fractions over 3 weeks to the whole breast with or without regional nodes, with a simultaneous tumor-bed boost of 48 Gy in 15 fractions (3.2 Gy per fraction).

NCT04025164.schema_source: Open-access protocol, Jin et al., Radiation Oncology 2024 (PMID 38802888). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Women aged 18 to 70 with invasive breast cancer, pathologic T1 to T3 and N0 to N3, M0, a single tumor or multiple tumors removable by one quadrantectomy, negative margins, and no distant metastasis before radiotherapy.

Sentinel-node biopsy and/or axillary dissection. A positive sentinel node requires level I and II dissection with at least 10 nodes. The tumor bed must be identifiable by clips or postoperative CT changes. Receptor and Ki-67 status by immunohistochemistry. KPS at least 80. Written consent.

Excluded: T4 or distant metastasis, suspected or confirmed supraclavicular or internal mammary metastasis, pure DCIS, bilateral cancer, neoadjuvant systemic therapy, prior ipsilateral breast or nodal irradiation, pregnancy or lactation, active infection, prior malignancy other than non-melanoma skin cancer or cervical carcinoma in situ, and KPS 70 or lower.

followup.item: Routine visits
followup.window: Every 3 months in year 1, every 6 months in years 2 to 5, then annually
followup.note: Acute toxicity before, during, at the end of, and 3 months after radiotherapy, graded by CTCAE 4.03 and the RTOG scale. Late toxicity before radiotherapy, at 3 months, and then annually, using RTOG late morbidity and LENT-SOMA scales.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-arm multicenter phase II trial (TROG 15.03 FASTRACK II) of definitive SABR for biopsy-confirmed primary renal cell carcinoma. Target accrual is 70 patients over 3 years, with follow-up to 5 years from the end of accrual. Primary endpoint is freedom from local progression at 1 year, with a hypothesis that it exceeds 80%.

schema.label: Treatment
schema.text: All treated participants receive SABR. Fractionation depends on tumor size. Prescription is to the covering isodose so that 99% of the PTV receives 100% of the dose, or 95% if organ-at-risk limits cannot otherwise be met. Peak dose is ideally 125% and must not exceed 143%. Fractions are on non-consecutive days and finish within 3 weeks. A 4DCT and at least a half-body vacuum immobilizer are required.

arms.label: Tumor 4 cm or smaller
arms.text: 26 Gy in one fraction.

arms.label: Tumor larger than 4 cm
arms.text: 42 Gy in three fractions.

NCT02613819.schema_source: Open-access protocol, Siva et al., BMC Cancer 2018 (PMID 30352550). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Age at least 18, biopsy-confirmed RCC with no more than one lesion in a kidney (bilateral RCC is allowed), ECOG 2 or lower, life expectancy more than 9 months, and a multidisciplinary decision that active treatment is warranted.
Medically inoperable, technically high risk for surgery, or declines surgery. Written consent.

Excluded: pretreatment eGFR below 30 mL/min, prior systemic therapy for RCC, prior overlapping high-dose radiotherapy (BED above 40 Gy, alpha/beta 10), tumor larger than 10 cm, direct bowel contact, untreated prior malignancy or a prior malignancy within 2 years, visceral or bone metastases, and horseshoe kidney. The published list joins the ECOG criterion to the biopsy bullet.

followup.item: Split-function renal imaging
followup.window: Baseline and 12, 24, 42, and 60 months
followup.note: DMSA SPECT/CT for each enrolled patient. Serious adverse events are reported from the start of radiotherapy until 90 days after the last fraction.

specimens.window: Baseline, 3 months, and 12 months in a subset
specimens.note: Diffusion-weighted and dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI, correlated with RECIST tumor change.

submission.label: Radiotherapy quality assurance
submission.text: Credentialing includes a phantom dosimetry audit, facility questionnaire, and plan benchmark. A pre-treatment technical review checks targets, organs at risk, and plan quality, with post-treatment review of all cases.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Investigator-initiated, rater-blinded, multicenter national phase III trial (ESCALOX) of dose-escalated SIB-IMRT versus conventional SIB-IMRT, both with concurrent cisplatin, for locally advanced squamous cell carcinoma of the oral cavity, oropharynx, or hypopharynx. A 20-patient safety pre-study precedes the main study, which plans 250 subjects. Primary question is a 15% gain in 2-year locoregional control.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: IMRT or VMAT with simultaneous integrated boost. Cisplatin may be 40 mg/m2 weekly for up to 6 doses, or 20 mg/m2 per day on days 1 to 5 of weeks 1 and 5 (cumulative 200 mg/m2). Weekly carboplatin AUC 2 is allowed if renal function falls. Elective nodal CTV is the 56 Gy level in both arms.

arms.label: Arm A
arms.text: Dose escalation of macroscopic tumor and involved nodes at least 2 cm, up to 80.5 Gy.

arms.label: Arm B
arms.text: Standard simultaneous integrated boost up to 70.0 Gy.

NCT01212354.schema_source: Open-access protocol, Pigorsch et al. 2017 (PMID 28249612). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Locally advanced non-resectable head and neck squamous cell carcinoma of the oral cavity, oropharynx, or hypopharynx. The full inclusion and exclusion list is Table 1 and is not restated. Non-resectable means a very low probability of R0 resection, confirmed by ENT, oral surgery, radiation oncology, radiology, and pathology.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: NSGO-9501/EORTC 55991 randomized trial of pelvic radiotherapy with or without adjuvant chemotherapy for high-risk endometrial cancer after hysterectomy. The report also describes the parallel MaNGO ILIADE-III study. This brief uses only the NSGO/EORTC trial as printed.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: NSGO randomization used blocks stratified by center and histology. EORTC used minimization with the same factors.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Central randomization. Optional vaginal brachytherapy had to be chosen before randomization. Initially radiotherapy preceded chemotherapy. Amendment 1 allowed the sequence to be chosen before randomization.

arms.label: Radiotherapy
arms.text: Pelvic radiotherapy according to departmental guidelines, at least 44 Gy.

arms.label: Radiotherapy plus chemotherapy
arms.text: The same pelvic radiotherapy plus four courses of doxorubicin or epirubicin 50 mg/m2 and cisplatin 50 mg/m2 every 4 weeks. From August 2004, paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 plus epirubicin 60 mg/m2 or doxorubicin 40 mg/m2 and carboplatin AUC 5, or paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 plus carboplatin AUC 5 to 6 every 3 weeks, was also allowed.

NCT00005583.schema_source: Trial report, Hogberg et al., Eur J Cancer 2010 (PMID 20619634). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Histologically verified endometrial cancer, hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, lymphadenectomy optional, no residual macroscopic tumor, FIGO 1988 surgical stage I, age 80 or younger, WHO performance status below 3, and adequate marrow, liver, and kidney function.
Risk profile based on stage, grade, and myometrial invasion. Many Swedish departments also used DNA ploidy.
Amendment 1 also allowed occult stage II, stage IIIA limited to positive cytology, and stage IIIC limited to positive pelvic nodes without macroscopic residual tumor.

followup.item: Clinical follow-up
followup.window: 3 and 6 months after treatment, then every 6 months for 5 years
followup.note: Gynecologic examination at each visit. Chest radiograph annually.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Open-label intergroup phase III trial (EORTC 10994/BIG 1-00, NCT00017095) of neoadjuvant chemotherapy in large operable, locally advanced, or inflammatory breast cancer, testing whether taxane benefit is concentrated in p53-mutant tumors. Primary endpoint is progression-free survival. A frozen pretreatment tumor sample was mandatory.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Minimization by institution and initial stage (large operable versus locally advanced or inflammatory).

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Central 1:1 randomization. Nine Swedish centers used tailored FEC in the control arm. Other centers used FEC100. Exact milligram doses are referred to a figure and are not restated.

arms.label: Arm A, anthracycline
arms.text: Standard anthracycline regimen: FEC100, or tailored FEC in the Swedish centers.

arms.label: Arm B, taxane
arms.text: Three cycles of docetaxel, then three cycles of epirubicin plus docetaxel.

NCT00017095.schema_source: Trial report, Bonnefoi et al., The Lancet Oncology 2011 (PMID 21570352). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Large operable, locally advanced, or inflammatory breast cancer, with signed consent for the trial and for research on a pretreatment tumor sample.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Prospective multicenter randomized phase III protocol (ESO-Shanghai 1). Planned enrollment is 436. Primary comparison is paclitaxel plus fluorouracil versus cisplatin plus fluorouracil, both with definitive chemoradiotherapy.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Central 1:1 randomization stratified by investigator center.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Both arms receive involved-field IMRT, 61.2 Gy in 34 fractions of 1.8 Gy, 5 days per week, photons of 6 MV.

arms.label: Arm A, PF
arms.text: Two concurrent and two consolidation 28-day cycles: 5-FU 1800 mg/m2 continuous infusion over 72 hours on day 1 and cisplatin 25 mg/m2 per day on days 1 to 3.

arms.label: Arm B, TF
arms.text: Five weekly concurrent cycles of 5-FU 300 mg/m2 over 96 hours and paclitaxel 50 mg/m2 on day 1, then two monthly consolidation cycles of 5-FU 1800 mg/m2 over 72 hours and paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 on day 1.

NCT01591135.schema_source: Open-access protocol, Chen et al., Radiation Oncology 2018 (PMID 29482649). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Age 18 to 75, pathologic esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, AJCC 2002 T2N0M0 through TxNxM1a, no prior radiotherapy or chemotherapy, ECOG 0 to 2, life expectancy more than 3 months, and the printed blood, liver, and kidney thresholds.

Excluded: complete obstruction, deep ulcer, perforation, or hematemesis; prior esophageal radiotherapy or chemotherapy; surgery within 28 days; M1b disease; another interventional trial within 30 days; pregnancy or breastfeeding; addiction or AIDS; uncontrolled seizures or psychiatric disease; prior malignancy other than basal-cell skin cancer or cervical carcinoma in situ with at least 3 years disease-free.

pretreatment.item: Baseline staging
pretreatment.window: Blood tests within 14 days before enrollment
pretreatment.note: Endoscopy with biopsy, chest CT and abdominal and neck ultrasound (CT or MRI acceptable), fine-needle aspiration of superficial nodal metastases, and history with height and weight.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-arm phase I/II trial (FASTR-2) of prostate-only stereotactic radiotherapy plus 18 months of androgen deprivation for high-risk prostate cancer. The aim is safety. Biochemical disease-free survival is secondary.

schema.label: Treatment
schema.text: CTV is the prostate plus at least the proximal 1 cm of seminal vesicles. Five fractions, one per week. Cone-beam CT soft-tissue match to the prostate before each fraction. Rectal spacers were not used.

arms.label: FASTR-2
arms.text: 35 Gy in 5 weekly fractions to the prostate, with 18 months of androgen deprivation. Pelvic nodes are not irradiated.

NCT02229734.schema_source: Trial report, Callan et al. 2019 (PMID 31681864). Read from the full text.
eligibility: At least one NCCN high-risk feature: cT3 or T4, PSA above 20, or Gleason score at least 8 on transrectal biopsy.
No metastases on pelvic CT or bone scan, and able to comply with visits and treatment.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-arm phase II trial (ESO-Shanghai 7) at Fudan University Shanghai Cancer Center of definitive radiotherapy plus S-1 for previously untreated locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma in patients who refused or could not receive intravenous chemotherapy.

schema.label: Treatment
schema.text: Involved-field IMRT. S-1 starts on day 1 of radiotherapy and is given orally on days 1 to 28. Dose is 40 mg twice daily if body surface area is under 1.6 m2, and 50 mg twice daily if it is at least 1.6 m2. A powder form is allowed if capsules cannot be swallowed.

arms.label: S-1 plus radiotherapy
arms.text: 61.2 Gy in 34 fractions of 1.8 Gy, 5 fractions per week, prescribed at the isocenter with 6 MV photons, plus the S-1 schedule above.

NCT01831531.schema_source: Trial report, Chen et al., Frontiers in Oncology 2022 (PMID 35449578). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Histologically confirmed esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, stage IIa to IVa, previously untreated, and either older than 75 or intolerant of intravenous chemotherapy because of serious comorbidity.
ECOG 0 to 2, life expectancy at least 3 months, the printed organ-function thresholds, and effective contraception.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-center, open-label phase II trial (ETNT) of response-adapted therapy after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy for locally advanced resectable thoracic esophageal squamous cell carcinoma. Primary endpoint is pathologic complete response in the non-complete-response population.

schema.label: Treatment
schema.text: All patients start with neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy. Response is assessed by RECIST 1.1. Clinical complete response is judged by the multidisciplinary team 4 weeks after chemoradiotherapy, using contrast CT, endoscopic biopsy, bronchoscopy, ultrasound endoscopy, cervical ultrasound, and MRI.

arms.label: Induction for all patients
arms.text: Paclitaxel 135 mg/m2 on day 1 and carboplatin AUC 3 to 5 on day 1, every 3 weeks for two cycles, with radiotherapy 40 Gy in 20 fractions over 4 weeks.

arms.label: Clinical complete response
arms.text: Surgery 4 to 6 weeks later. After an R0 resection, pathologic complete responders undergo surveillance. Patients without a pathologic complete response receive tislelizumab 200 mg every 21 days for 1 year.

arms.label: Partial response or stable disease
arms.text: Two cycles of paclitaxel 135 mg/m2, carboplatin AUC 3 to 5, and tislelizumab 200 mg, all on day 1, every 3 weeks, then surgery 4 to 6 weeks later. After an R0 resection, pathologic complete responders undergo surveillance and the others receive tislelizumab 200 mg every 21 days for 1 year.

arms.label: Progression or non-R0 resection
arms.text: Clinical progression, or failure to achieve an R0 resection, is managed with a new regimen after multidisciplinary discussion.

NCT05189730.schema_source: Trial report, He et al., Frontiers in Immunology 2022 (PMID 35720312). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Histologically confirmed locally advanced resectable thoracic esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, AJCC 8th edition T1-4a N+ or T3-4a N0, age 18 to 75, at least one RECIST 1.1 lesion, ECOG 0 or 1, expected survival more than 6 months, no other cancer and no prior anticancer therapy, and no operative contraindication.
Printed marrow, liver, kidney, and thyroid thresholds, and contraception for women of childbearing potential.

Excluded: distant metastasis, infection needing treatment, active autoimmune disease or systemic steroids above prednisone 10 mg daily, clinically significant effusion, uncontrolled cardiac disease, abnormal coagulation or recent bleeding or thromboembolism, significant gastrointestinal bleeding risk, interstitial or other severe lung disease, HIV or active hepatitis, another trial, live vaccine within 4 weeks, and psychiatric or substance-abuse history.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-arm phase II trial (ESO-Shanghai 9) of extensive-field postoperative chemoradiotherapy after radical transthoracic resection of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.

schema.label: Treatment
schema.text: Radiotherapy starts on day 1 with cycle 1 of chemotherapy. Five weekly chemotherapy cycles are planned. Involved margins of the PTV are 1 cm beyond the CTV, with a small cord-side adjustment allowed.

arms.label: Extended-field chemoradiotherapy
arms.text: IMRT, at least 6 MV, 45 Gy in 25 fractions of 1.8 Gy, 5 days per week. CTV includes the tumor bed, anastomosis, bilateral supraclavicular regions, all mediastinal nodal stations, and left gastric and celiac nodes. Weekly paclitaxel 50 mg/m2 and carboplatin AUC 2 on day 1.

NCT02916511.schema_source: Trial report, Ai et al., Radiation Oncology 2023 (PMID 36750858). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Radical transthoracic resection with negative margins within 3 months, pT3-4 any N M0 or any T N+ M0 (AJCC 7th edition). No preoperative radiotherapy or chemotherapy. No locoregional recurrence or distant metastasis before enrollment.

Age 75 or younger, KPS at least 80, neutrophils at least 1.5 x 10^9/L, leukocytes at least 3 x 10^9/L, platelets at least 100 x 10^9/L, creatinine below 1.5 times the upper limit, and ALT or AST below 2.5 times the upper limit.

during.note: Radiotherapy pauses for grade 3 or higher toxicity until recovery to grade 2 or lower. Chemotherapy on day 1 of a cycle is held for neutrophils below 1.5 x 10^9/L, platelets below 100 x 10^9/L, or grade 2 or higher non-hematologic toxicity.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-arm phase II study (ESFT13) adding window and maintenance therapy to interval-compressed chemotherapy for high-risk Ewing sarcoma. Two-stage design: continue past 12 patients if at least 7 of 12 have a WHO complete or partial response. Primary endpoint is that WHO response after two window cycles.

schema.label: Treatment
schema.text: Local control after cycle 6 is individualized: surgery, surgery plus radiation, radiation, or radiation then surgery. Radiation doses are only in Supplemental Table S1 and are not restated. All patients with lung metastases at diagnosis receive whole-lung irradiation. Unresected metastatic sites larger than 1 cm, and residual unresectable lung lesions larger than 1 cm, receive additional radiotherapy, including an SBRT boost for residual lung lesions. Doses for those boosts are not printed in the main text.

arms.label: ESFT13 regimen
arms.text: Two 21-day window cycles of irinotecan 20 mg/m2 IV on days 1 to 5 and 8 to 12, temozolomide 100 mg/m2 orally on days 1 to 5, and temsirolimus 35 mg/m2 IV on days 1 and 8. Then 13 cycles of interval-compressed VDC/IE. A partial response or better to window therapy substitutes ITT for IE in cycles 11 and 12. Patients with stable disease or better may receive six 21-day maintenance cycles: BEV 15 mg/kg IV on day 1, SOR 90 mg/m2 orally twice daily on days 1 to 21, and poCY 50 mg/m2 orally daily on days 1 to 21. The paper uses those abbreviations.

NCT01946529.schema_source: Trial report, Gartrell et al., Cancers 2025 (PMID 40940991). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Age 25 or younger with newly diagnosed high-risk Ewing sarcoma. High risk means age at least 14, a pelvic primary, or metastatic disease. Informed consent.

followup.item: Response imaging and quality of life
followup.window: PET at diagnosis, week 6, week 12, and end of treatment. Quality of life at diagnosis, before local control, end of induction, end of therapy, and 1, 2, 5, and 10 years off therapy
followup.note: WHO criteria after window therapy. Later response uses volumetric criteria and RECIST 1.1. Toxicity by CTCAE v4.0.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: The paper reports postoperative chemoradiotherapy from ESO-Shanghai 17 and a joint analysis with related phase II trials. ESO-Shanghai 17 is the small T-shaped field trial. Primary endpoint of these studies is 2-year local control, defined as no recurrence at the anastomosis or regional nodes.

schema.label: Treatment
schema.text: Radiotherapy starts on day 1 with the first chemotherapy cycle. Five cycles of weekly paclitaxel 50 mg/m2 and carboplatin AUC 2 are scheduled. The sentence pairs 50.4 Gy in 28 fractions with ESO-Shanghai 17 and 45 Gy in 25 fractions with ESO-Shanghai 9.

arms.label: ESO-Shanghai 17
arms.text: IMRT, photons of at least 6 MV, 50.4 Gy in 28 fractions of 1.8 Gy, 5 days per week, to a small T-shaped field, with the weekly paclitaxel and carboplatin.

NCT04764227.schema_source: Trial report, Shen et al., Clinical and Translational Radiation Oncology 2026 (PMID 41531940). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Radical surgery with negative margins within 3 months, esophageal squamous cell carcinoma pT3-4 any N M0 or any T N+ M0 (AJCC 8th edition). No preoperative chemoradiotherapy. No local recurrence or metastasis before enrollment.

Age 18 to 75, ECOG 0 or 1, neutrophils at least 1.5 x 10^9/L, leukocytes at least 3 x 10^9/L, platelets at least 100 x 10^9/L, creatinine below 1.5 times the upper limit, and ALT or AST below 2.5 times the upper limit.

during.note: Grade 3 or higher toxicity pauses radiotherapy until recovery to grade 2 or lower. Day-1 chemotherapy is held for neutrophils below 1.5 x 10^9/L, platelets below 100 x 10^9/L, or grade 2 or higher non-hematologic toxicity.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Updated individual-patient combined analysis of RTOG 9501 and EORTC 22931. This brief records only the EORTC 22931 design as printed (NCT00002555). Radiation dose is not restated in the sections read.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Both trials randomized patients with oral cavity, larynx, hypopharynx, or oropharynx cancer after resection to postoperative radiotherapy with or without cisplatin.

arms.label: Radiotherapy
arms.text: Postoperative radiotherapy alone. The dose is not printed in this paper.

arms.label: Chemoradiotherapy
arms.text: The same postoperative radiotherapy plus concomitant cisplatin 100 mg/m2 for 3 cycles.

NCT00002555.schema_source: Trial report, Zumsteg et al. 2025 (PMID 40680992). Read from the full text.
eligibility: The paper says EORTC 22931 eligibility is described in the original reports. It does not restate a full eligibility list. It does state the shared disease sites: oral cavity, larynx, hypopharynx, and oropharynx, after surgical resection.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Phase III FeDeriCa trial of intravenous pertuzumab plus trastuzumab versus a fixed-dose subcutaneous combination, with chemotherapy, for HER2-positive early breast cancer. This final analysis restates the design. Median follow-up at the 2 June 2023 cutoff was about 51 months.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Eight cycles of investigator-chosen neoadjuvant chemotherapy. HER2 antibodies are given every 3 weeks during cycles 5 to 8, randomized 1:1. Patients continue the same HER2 route in the adjuvant phase.

arms.label: Intravenous
arms.text: Pertuzumab 840 mg load then 420 mg, plus trastuzumab 8 mg/kg then 6 mg/kg, every 3 weeks.

arms.label: Subcutaneous fixed dose
arms.text: 1200 mg pertuzumab plus 600 mg trastuzumab in 15 mL as the load, then 600 mg of each in 10 mL, every 3 weeks.

NCT03493854.schema_source: Trial report, Jackisch et al. 2026 (PMID 42537585). Read from the full text.
eligibility: HER2-positive operable, locally advanced, or inflammatory stage II to IIIC breast cancer, age at least 18, primary tumor larger than 2 cm or node-positive disease, LVEF at least 55%, and ECOG 0 or 1. HER2 and hormone receptors confirmed centrally.

Ineligible after any systemic therapy for treatment or prevention of breast cancer, radiotherapy for this disease, a serious cardiac condition, or impaired liver function. The paper says the population was fully described previously.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Randomized, uncontrolled, blinded clinical trial of photobiomodulation in relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis. No placebo group was used. Participants continued their usual disease medication.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: After baseline examination and blood collection, participants were randomized to two active photobiomodulation groups. The same laser parameters were used in both: 808 nm, 100 mW, 0.40 cm diameter, 287 J/cm2, 360 seconds, twice weekly for 12 weeks (24 sessions).

arms.label: Group 1
arms.text: Sublingual photobiomodulation.

arms.label: Group 2
arms.text: Transcutaneous photobiomodulation over the radial artery.

NCT03360487.schema_source: Trial report, Silva et al., PLoS ONE 2020 (PMID 32255785). Read from the full text.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Prospective pilot cohort within the phase II FENET-2016 trial of peptide-receptor radionuclide therapy for advanced neuroendocrine neoplasms. The two activity schemes were chosen empirically for each patient. This paper does not describe a randomization between them.

schema.label: Treatment
schema.text: Two mutually exclusive [177Lu]Lu-DOTATOC schemes, with or without [90Y]Y-DOTATOC. Cycles are separated by 8 to 10 weeks.

arms.label: MONO
arms.text: Five cycles of 3.7 to 5.55 GBq of [177Lu]Lu-DOTATOC. Cumulative activity 18.5 to 27.75 GBq.

arms.label: DUO
arms.text: Three cycles of 3.7 to 5.55 GBq of [177Lu]Lu-DOTATOC alternating with two cycles of 1.85 to 2.75 GBq of [90Y]Y-DOTATOC. Cumulative activity 11.1 to 16.65 GBq of lutetium and 3.7 to 5.55 GBq of yttrium. Cycles are 8 to 10 weeks apart.

NCT04790708.schema_source: Trial report, Urso et al. 2022 (PMID 36297443). Read from the full text.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: The paper links routine National Cancer Registration and Analysis Service data to the UK TACT trial (CRUK01/001, NCT00033683). It restates the randomization but is not the protocol.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Between February 2001 and July 2003, 4162 women with node-positive or high-risk node-negative early breast cancer were randomized.

arms.label: FEC-T
arms.text: Sequential docetaxel after anthracycline chemotherapy (fluorouracil, epirubicin, and cyclophosphamide, then docetaxel).

arms.label: Anthracycline control
arms.text: Standard anthracycline chemotherapy of similar duration: FEC, or epirubicin followed by cyclophosphamide, methotrexate, and fluorouracil (E-CMF).

NCT00033683.schema_source: Trial report, Kilburn et al. 2017 (PMID 29179731). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Women with node-positive or high-risk node-negative early breast cancer.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Joint final report of EORTC 26951 and RTOG 9402. This brief uses the EORTC 26951 arm description only. Stratification factors are said to have been published previously and are not restated.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Open-label randomized phase III comparison of radiotherapy with or without PCV for newly diagnosed anaplastic oligodendroglial tumors. Radiotherapy in both studies was 59.4 Gy in 33 fractions of 1.8 Gy.

arms.label: Radiotherapy
arms.text: 59.4 Gy in 33 fractions of 1.8 Gy.

arms.label: Radiotherapy plus PCV
arms.text: The same radiotherapy followed by up to six cycles of adjuvant procarbazine, lomustine, and vincristine. The paper does not restate the PCV milligram doses.

NCT00002840.schema_source: Trial report, Lassman et al. 2022 (PMID 35731991). Read from the full text.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: EORTC 22042-26042 (NCT00626730) studies high-dose radiotherapy for atypical (WHO grade II) or malignant (WHO grade III) meningioma. The quality-assurance paper describes one radiotherapy prescription for all patients rather than a randomized comparison. Endpoints include progression-free survival, tolerance, and global cognitive function.

schema.label: Treatment
schema.text: 3D conformal radiotherapy or IMRT, photons 4 to 20 MV, 2 Gy per fraction once daily. Postoperative MRI was required. GTV is visible tumor on fused gadolinium T1 MRI and planning CT, including thickened dural tails and hyperostotic bone.

arms.label: High-dose radiotherapy
arms.text: 60 Gy to PTV1 for every patient. If Simpson stage is greater than 3, an additional 10 Gy boost follows. The boost volume is not fully specified in the extracted sentence.

NCT00626730.schema_source: Trial report, Coskun et al. 2013 (PMID 23363568). Read from the full text.

submission.label: Digital plan submission
submission.text: Dummy-run and individual case plans were submitted to the Image-Guided Therapy QA Center of the Advanced Technology Consortium.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: This is a systematic review of phase III glioblastoma trials. It restates the EORTC/NCIC trial that corresponds to EORTC 26981-22981 (NCT00006353). The radiotherapy dose in gray is not printed in the paragraph read.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: 573 patients aged 18 to 70 were randomized after histologic confirmation. 286 were assigned to the control arm and 287 to the temozolomide arm.

arms.label: Radiotherapy
arms.text: Radiotherapy alone.

arms.label: Radiotherapy plus temozolomide
arms.text: Temozolomide 75 mg/m2 daily during radiotherapy, for no more than 49 days. After a 4-week break, temozolomide on days 1 to 5 of each 28-day cycle for six cycles.

NCT00006353.schema_source: Open-access review, Oster et al. 2023 (PMID 37811538). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Adults aged 18 to 70 with newly diagnosed glioblastoma, as stated for the EORTC/NCIC trial in this review.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-arm prospective study (HAMA-M1-C001, NCT00197444) of daily low-dose nedaplatin and continuous 5-fluorouracil with radiotherapy for esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.

schema.label: Treatment
schema.text: Nedaplatin 10 mg/body/day and 5-FU 500 mg/body/day as a continuous infusion for 20 days, given with fractionated radiotherapy. Radiotherapy starts on the first day of chemotherapy, five days a week, at 1.8 to 2.0 Gy per fraction, to a total dose of 50.4 to 66 Gy. After 40 Gy the field is changed to avoid the spinal cord, except in two patients. Additional nedaplatin and 5-FU after chemoradiotherapy is optional, for a maximum of five courses.

NCT00197444.schema_source: Open-access trial report, Osawa et al., BMC Cancer 2009 (PMID 19930599). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Clinical stage I to IVB esophageal squamous cell carcinoma. Thirty-three patients were enrolled between January 2003 and June 2008.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: This paper analyzes patients aged 60 years or older in the randomized phase III trial E2496 (NCT00003389). The trial itself compared ABVD with Stanford V, with radiotherapy for selected bulky disease. The primary endpoint of E2496 was failure-free survival.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients were randomized to ABVD or Stanford V.

arms.label: ABVD
arms.text: ABVD (adriamycin, bleomycin, vinblastine, and dacarbazine) every 28 days for six or eight cycles, depending on the CT response. Patients with bulky mediastinal adenopathy received 36 Gy to the mediastinum, bilateral hila, and bilateral supraclavicular areas, starting two weeks after chemotherapy.

arms.label: Stanford V
arms.text: Stanford V for 12 weeks, with prophylactic trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole and ketoconazole. Radiotherapy of 36 Gy was given for bulky mediastinal adenopathy and also to any pretreatment site larger than 5 cm and to macroscopic splenic disease on CT.

NCT00003389.schema_source: Trial report, Evens et al., British Journal of Haematology 2013 (PMID 23356491). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Classical Hodgkin lymphoma, previously untreated, advanced stage III or IV, or local disease with a bulky mediastinal mass larger than one third of the maximum intrathoracic diameter on a standing posteroanterior chest radiograph.

schema.label: Design
