schema.text: Phase III trial S0001 (NCT00017147) of radiotherapy plus O6-benzylguanine and BCNU versus radiotherapy plus BCNU in newly diagnosed glioblastoma or gliosarcoma. The primary endpoint was overall survival.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Dynamic balancing by age (under 50 versus 50 or older), Zubrod performance status (0 to 1 versus 2), and surgery (biopsy only versus resection).

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Treatment started within five working days of registration. Chemotherapy began concurrently with radiotherapy. A maximum of seven cycles was allowed.

arms.label: O6-BG plus BCNU and radiotherapy
arms.text: O6-BG 120 mg/m2 intravenously over one hour, then six hours later BCNU 40 mg/m2, every six weeks, plus radiotherapy.

arms.label: BCNU and radiotherapy
arms.text: BCNU 200 mg/m2 intravenously over one hour every six weeks, plus radiotherapy.

schema.label: Treatment
schema.text: Radiotherapy was once daily, five days a week, with at least 4 MV photons and multiple conformal fields, without intensity modulation. The initial volume was T2 signal plus a 2 cm margin, treated to 50.4 Gy in 28 fractions. The boost was the resection cavity plus gadolinium enhancement plus a 2.5 cm margin, treated with an additional 10.8 Gy in 6 fractions, for 61.2 Gy cumulative.

NCT00017147.schema_source: Trial report, Blumenthal et al., International Journal of Clinical Oncology 2014 (PMID 25407559). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Histologically confirmed glioblastoma or gliosarcoma, age at least 18, Zubrod performance status 2 or better, and biopsy or resection within 28 days before registration.

Adequate renal function (creatinine at or below 1.5 times the upper limit of normal, or creatinine clearance at least 60 mL/min) and PT/PTT at or below 120% of the upper limit of normal. Pulmonary function required DLCO at least 70% of predicted.

Excluded: prior or concurrent cranial radiotherapy or chemotherapy outside the protocol; three or more noncontiguous T2 sites; known allergy to the study drugs; HIV; uncontrolled medical illness; specified prior malignancy; pregnancy or nursing.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Double-blind randomized trial (FLAIR, NCT02002052) of standard radiotherapy versus functional lung-avoidance radiotherapy. Both arms use the same prescription dose. The concurrent chemotherapy regimen is not named in the protocol.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients are randomized 1:1 in permuted blocks after two clinically approved plans have been prepared. The radiation oncologist is blinded to machine parameters until the assigned plan is selected.

arms.label: Standard radiotherapy
arms.text: 60 Gy in 30 fractions. At least 95% of the PTV receives 95% of the prescription. The plan ignores functional ventilation.

arms.label: Functional lung avoidance
arms.text: The same 60 Gy in 30 fractions and the same technique (VMAT, static-gantry IMRT, or tomotherapy; rotation preferred). Dose to ventilated lung is minimized, aiming to lower V5, V20, and mean dose in functional lung, while keeping the anatomical-lung V20 of the two plans within 3% of each other.

NCT02002052.schema_source: Open-access protocol, Hoover et al., BMC Cancer 2014 (PMID 25496482). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Stage III non-small cell lung cancer with intent to receive concurrent chemoradiotherapy. Every patient undergoes pretreatment hyperpolarized 3He MRI to map ventilated lung.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Two-arm open-label randomized phase II trial (GlioCave/NOA-17, NCT02715297) testing whether stereotactic fractionated radiotherapy to the resection cavity improves progression-free survival after resection of recurrent glioblastoma, compared with observation.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Eligible patients are randomized 1:1.

arms.label: Arm A, radiotherapy
arms.text: Postoperative stereotactic fractionated radiotherapy, 46 Gy in 2 Gy fractions or 36 Gy in 3 Gy fractions, chosen by the size and location of the target. The prescription is to 95% of the PTV.

arms.label: Arm B, observation
arms.text: Observation after resection, without adjuvant radiotherapy.

NCT02715297.schema_source: Open-access protocol, Straube et al., BMC Cancer 2018 (PMID 29298660). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Recurrent glioblastoma after resection. The printed methods refer to inclusion and exclusion criteria without listing laboratory cutoffs in the extracted text.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Non-randomized phase II trial (SABR-5, NCT02933242). All participants receive stereotactic ablative radiotherapy to every site of progressing metastatic disease. The accrual target is 200 patients. The primary concern stated in the protocol is toxicity.

schema.label: Treatment
schema.text: SABR is delivered to all sites of active metastatic disease, with a maximum of five metastases. For non-brainstem metastases, single-fraction radiosurgery is limited to a maximum size of 3 cm. Lesions from 3.1 to 4 cm may be treated with 25 to 35 Gy in 5 fractions. Brain cases require stereotactic rounds approval. Other site-specific doses are printed in a protocol table whose grid did not extract as a reliable dose list, so those rows are not restated. The PTV volume receiving 100% of the prescription should equal 95%, and coverage may be reduced to meet organ-at-risk constraints. Patients are excluded if 100% coverage falls below 50% of the PTV.

NCT02933242.schema_source: Open-access protocol, Olson et al., BMC Cancer 2018 (PMID 30286739). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Age 18 or older, histologically confirmed malignancy, and at most five metastases eligible for SABR. The primary tumor has been treated radically or controlled by prior palliative radiotherapy or systemic therapy. Biopsy of a metastasis is preferred but not required.

Excluded: comorbidity precluding radiotherapy; femoral metastasis at high risk of fracture; one to three brain metastases and no disease elsewhere; complete response to first-line chemotherapy; persistent malignant pleural effusion; inability to treat every site of progressing disease; spinal cord compression; a dominant brain metastasis requiring surgical decompression; pregnancy or lactation.

during.window: From 48 hours before the first fraction until 48 hours after the last fraction
during.note: Cytotoxic, immunotherapy, or molecularly targeted agents are held. Some agents require a longer break. Hormonal therapy during SABR is allowed.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Randomized trial (NCT03346460) of tongue scraping and antimicrobial photodynamic therapy with Bixa orellana extract and LED light for halitosis. Thirty-nine participants are divided by block randomization into three groups of 13.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Participants are assigned to one of three treatments.

arms.label: Group 1, scraping
arms.text: Tongue scraping by one operator, with instruction on home use of the scraper.

arms.label: Group 2, photodynamic therapy
arms.text: One session of Bixa orellana extract at 20% sprayed over the middle third and back of the tongue, two minutes of pre-irradiation time, then six points on the tongue dorsum about 1 cm apart. The LED device is calibrated at 395 to 480 nm for 20 seconds and 9.6 J per point.

arms.label: Group 3, scraping plus photodynamic therapy
arms.text: Tongue scraping plus the same photodynamic therapy used in group 2.

NCT03346460.schema_source: Open-access protocol, Gonçalves et al., Trials 2018 (PMID 30373650). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Women and men aged 18 to 25 years with volatile sulphur compounds of at least 112 ppb on Oral Chroma.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: This MRI paper restates the randomized phase II GRECCAR 4 trial (NCT01333709). After four weeks of induction chemotherapy, patients were split by MRI response and then randomized within each stratum. Companion drugs and doses for the induction chemotherapy are not printed in this paper.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Stratum I was a favorable response: tumor-volume shrinkage of at least 75% and predicted CRM greater than 1 mm. Stratum II was shrinkage under 75% or predicted CRM of 1 mm or less. Randomization in stratum II stopped after the planned Cap60 patients were enrolled.

arms.label: Stratum I, arm A
arms.text: Immediate surgery.

arms.label: Stratum I, arm B
arms.text: Cap50 chemoradiotherapy, then surgery. Cap50 is 50 Gy at 2 Gy per fraction, five fractions a week for five weeks: 44 Gy to a mini-pelvic volume plus a 6 Gy boost, with oral capecitabine 1600 mg/m2 daily in two doses on radiotherapy days.

arms.label: Stratum II, arm C
arms.text: The same Cap50 regimen.

arms.label: Stratum II, arm D
arms.text: Cap60: 60 Gy at 2 Gy per fraction, five fractions a week for six weeks, as 44 Gy mini-pelvic radiotherapy plus a 16 Gy boost, with the same capecitabine schedule.

NCT01333709.schema_source: Trial report, Nougaret et al., The British Journal of Surgery 2019 (PMID 31436325). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Primary rectal tumor that was mriT3c or higher, mriT4, or had a predicted CRM of 1 mm or less. Age at least 18, ECOG 0 to 2, and adequate hematologic, hepatic, and renal function. The numeric laboratory limits are not printed.
Excluded: indication for immediate surgery, no MRI of the primary tumor, prior pelvic radiotherapy, or a contraindication to radiotherapy or chemotherapy.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Prospective non-randomized multicenter phase II trial (GAZAI, NCT03341520) of response-adapted involved-site radiotherapy plus obinutuzumab for early-stage nodal follicular lymphoma. The aim is to see whether 4 Gy plus obinutuzumab can avoid a conventional full radiotherapy dose.

schema.label: Treatment
schema.text: Obinutuzumab 1000 mg intravenously each week in weeks 1 to 4, then in weeks 8, 12, and 16. Involved-site radiotherapy of 2 Gy on two consecutive days is given in week 9, after the fifth obinutuzumab dose. Restaging is at week 18. If a metabolic complete response and morphologic partial response or better is not reached, salvage radiotherapy adds 18 fractions of 2 Gy, five fractions a week, starting in week 20, without further obinutuzumab.

NCT03341520.schema_source: Open-access protocol, König et al., Trials 2019 (PMID 31470902). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Age at least 18, ECOG 0 to 2, centrally reviewed CD20-positive follicular lymphoma grade 1 or 2, Ann Arbor stage I or II, nodal disease 7 cm or smaller, and no prior treatment. Staging includes FDG-PET/CT.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: This secondary analysis restates CALGB 80101 (NCT00052910), a randomized phase III comparison of two adjuvant chemoradiotherapy schedules after resection of non-metastatic gastric cancer. Drug milligram doses and the radiotherapy dose in gray are not printed in this paper.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients were assigned to one of two postoperative schedules. The cohort in this analysis was almost equally divided between the arms.

arms.label: Fluorouracil and leucovorin
arms.text: 5-fluorouracil plus leucovorin for 5 days on cycles 1, 3, and 4, and continuous intravenous 5-fluorouracil for 5 weeks in cycle 2 given concurrently with radiotherapy.

arms.label: ECF
arms.text: Epirubicin, cisplatin, and 5-fluorouracil for cycles 1, 3, and 4, and the same 5-week continuous intravenous 5-fluorouracil with concurrent radiotherapy in cycle 2.

NCT00052910.schema_source: Trial report, Abdel-Rahman et al., World Journal of Gastrointestinal Oncology 2019 (PMID 31908720). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Resected non-metastatic gastric cancer. Patients were included regardless of the extent of nodal dissection. Detailed eligibility is not restated in this secondary analysis.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Multicenter randomized phase III trial (RACE, NCT04375605) of perioperative FLOT versus induction FLOT followed by chemoradiotherapy, each followed by resection and postoperative FLOT, for resectable adenocarcinoma of the gastroesophageal junction. The primary endpoint is progression-free survival.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Allocation is 1:1, stratified by primary tumor site (AEG type I versus AEG type II or III).

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Both arms use the same FLOT doses: 5-FU 2600 mg/m2, leucovorin 200 mg/m2, oxaliplatin 85 mg/m2, and docetaxel 50 mg/m2, each on day 1, every 2 weeks.

arms.label: Arm A, perioperative FLOT
arms.text: Four neoadjuvant cycles, resection 4 to 6 weeks after day 1 of the last neoadjuvant cycle, then four adjuvant cycles starting 6 to 12 weeks after surgery.

arms.label: Investigational arm
arms.text: Two neoadjuvant FLOT cycles, then chemoradiotherapy beginning on day 21 after day 1 of the last chemotherapy cycle. Radiotherapy is 1.8 Gy per fraction, five fractions a week, to 45 Gy over 5 weeks, with weekly oxaliplatin 45 mg/m2 on days 1, 8, 15, 22, and 29 and continuous 5-FU 225 mg/m2. Resection is 4 to 6 weeks after the last chemoradiotherapy. Four adjuvant FLOT cycles start 6 to 12 weeks after surgery.

NCT04375605.schema_source: Open-access protocol, Lorenzen et al., BMC Cancer 2020 (PMID 32933498). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Histologically confirmed locally advanced, potentially resectable, non-metastatic adenocarcinoma of the gastroesophageal junction, AEG I to III: cT3 to 4 any N M0, or cT2 N+ M0, on the AJCC 8th edition. Candidates for curative resection, ECOG 0 or 1, age at least 18.

ANC at least 1.5 x 10^9/L, platelets at least 100 x 10^9/L, hemoglobin at least 9.0 mg/dl, INR below 1.5, aPTT below 1.5 times the upper limit of normal, transaminases at or below 2.5 times the upper limit, bilirubin at or below 1.5 times the upper limit, creatinine at or below 1.5 times the upper limit, and QTc (Bazett) at or below 440 ms.

Excluded: metastatic disease, another malignancy within 5 years, peripheral sensory neuropathy above grade 1, medical unfitness for chemotherapy or radiotherapy, and hypersensitivity or other printed contraindications to 5-FU, leucovorin, oxaliplatin, or docetaxel.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-center randomized phase II trial (HA-SIB-WBRT, NCT04452084) in multiple brain metastases. The target is 100 patients. The primary endpoint is time to target-lesion progression.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Stratified by fewer than 10 versus 10 or more brain metastases, then randomized 1:1. Patients and the treating radiation oncologist are not blinded.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Plans that cannot meet constraints are not eligible, and those patients leave the trial.

arms.label: Control, HA-WBRT
arms.text: Hippocampal-avoidance whole-brain radiotherapy, 30 Gy in 10 fractions.

arms.label: Experimental, HA-SIB-WBRT
arms.text: Hippocampal-avoidance whole-brain radiotherapy with a simultaneous integrated boost of 40 to 45 Gy in 10 fractions. 45 Gy is used in general. 40 Gy is used for tumors within or close to an organ at risk. Postoperative cavities are contoured. Daily image guidance is required.

NCT04452084.schema_source: Open-access protocol, Chia et al., BMC Cancer 2020 (PMID 33126867). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Good performance status, 4 to 25 brain metastases, and life expectancy longer than 6 months.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-institution unblinded randomized phase III superiority trial (NCT02323360) of stereotactic body radiotherapy versus a second course of TAE or TACE after an incomplete response of unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma to one prior TAE or TACE. The stereotactic dose in gray is not printed in this paper. The primary endpoint is local control.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: A minimization program with a random element balanced the groups for sex and Child-Pugh class.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients with BCLC A or B disease were randomized 1:1 after CT showed residual disease 6 to 8 weeks after the first TAE or TACE.

arms.label: SBRT
arms.text: Stereotactic body radiotherapy. The prescription dose is not printed.

arms.label: TAE or TACE
arms.text: A second course of bland embolization or conventional TACE. The paper does not print a required chemotherapy dose for the TACE arm.

NCT02323360.schema_source: Open-access trial report, Comito et al., Current Oncology 2022 (PMID 36421345). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Adults with Karnofsky performance status above 70% and unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma, diagnosed by histology or noninvasive EASL criteria, with radiologically defined residual disease after one prior TAE or TACE.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-arm phase II trial with safety stopping rules (GROINSS-V III, also NRG-GY024, NCT05076942) for macrometastatic sentinel-node disease in vulvar cancer. Inguinofemoral lymphadenectomy is not the study treatment.

schema.label: Treatment
schema.text: 48 to 50 Gy in 1.8 Gy daily fractions to the inguinofemoral and external iliac nodes, with a boost to the involved inguinal site to an equivalent dose of 56 Gy over 5 to 6 weeks. Concurrent cisplatin is 40 mg/m2 intravenously on days 1, 8, 15, 22, and 29. If creatinine clearance is 40 to 60 mL/min, cisplatin 20 mg/m2 or carboplatin AUC 2 may be used. Radiotherapy starts within 6 to 8 weeks of the primary surgery.

NCT05076942.schema_source: Study protocol, Gien et al., International Journal of Gynecological Cancer 2023 (PMID 36653060). Read from the full text.
eligibility: The sentinel-node procedure is for stage I, unifocal, invasive squamous cell carcinoma of the vulva, depth of invasion greater than 1 mm, tumor smaller than 4 cm, and no suspicious nodes on imaging.
Trial eligibility is a sentinel-node metastasis larger than 2 mm, extracapsular extension, or more than one sentinel node with micrometastasis of 2 mm or less.

Excluded: inoperable or larger than 4 cm tumors, multifocal tumors, non-squamous histology, enlarged or suspicious nodes on imaging (larger than 1.5 cm) or metastatic on fine-needle cytology, and prior pelvic radiotherapy.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Prospective open-label single-arm phase II trial (NCT02406105) of frameless CyberKnife radiosurgery for Parkinson disease tremor. The planned sample was 27 patients. The primary endpoint was safety.

schema.label: Treatment
schema.text: Single-fraction radiosurgery. The dose was prescribed as 100% at the central point, and the whole target was covered by the 80% isodose. The total dose ranged from 70 to 105 Gy and was escalated by 5 Gy after every three patients, with at least 3 months of toxicity observation before the next step.

NCT02406105.schema_source: Open-access trial report, Goc et al., Biomedicines 2023 (PMID 36830825). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Adults with idiopathic Parkinson disease by UK Brain Bank criteria, significant tremor, lack of effective pharmacotherapy, and a contraindication to deep-brain stimulation or refusal of that procedure. ECOG performance status no worse than 2. Patients had to understand the treatment and cooperate with the team.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-arm phase II trial (NCT01807611) of memory T-cell enriched haploidentical transplantation with NK-cell addback for high-risk hematologic malignancy without a matched donor.

schema.label: Treatment
schema.text: Conditioning was 8 Gy total-lymphoid irradiation in four equal fractions, fludarabine 30 mg/m2 for 5 days, cyclophosphamide 60 mg/kg for 1 day, thiotepa 5 mg/kg twice on 1 day, and melphalan 70 mg/m2 for 2 days. On day 0 patients received a G-CSF-mobilized CD34-enriched progenitor-cell graft, and on day 0 or day +1 a second, CD45RA-depleted graft. A purified NK-cell infusion was given on day +6.

NCT01807611.schema_source: Open-access trial report, Naik et al., Journal of Hematology & Oncology 2024 (PMID 38937803). Read from the full text.
eligibility: High-risk hematologic malignancy with an indication for transplant and no suitable HLA-matched donor. Complete remission included morphologic remission with flow-cytometric MRD below 0.1% for AML or below 0.01% for ALL. Active disease was more than 5% blasts by morphology.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Non-randomized two-cohort phase II study (GASTO-1071, NCT04844385) of neoadjuvant toripalimab plus chemotherapy followed by chemoradiotherapy for unresectable locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma. The cohorts were not randomized against each other. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival.

schema.label: Treatment
schema.text: Both cohorts received albumin-bound paclitaxel 260 mg/m2, nedaplatin 75 mg/m2, and toripalimab 240 mg on day 1 of each 3-week cycle for two cycles. Intensity-modulated radiotherapy then used 6 to 8 MV photons, five consecutive days a week. Cohort A received 60 Gy in 24 fractions. Cohort B received 50 Gy in 20 fractions. Concurrent oral capecitabine was given with radiotherapy. The capecitabine milligram dose is not printed.

NCT04844385.schema_source: Open-access trial report, Liu et al., eClinicalMedicine 2025 (PMID 40242562). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Unresectable esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, T1 to 4, N0 to 3, M0 to 1, with M1 limited to supraclavicular lymph-node metastasis. Age 18 to 80, ECOG 0 or 1, no prior chemotherapy, radiotherapy, surgery, targeted therapy, or immunotherapy, life expectancy at least 12 weeks, and adequate organ and marrow function. The numeric laboratory cutoffs are not printed in the extracted methods.
Excluded findings named in the methods include another malignancy and concurrent participation in another trial. The remainder of the exclusion list is truncated in the extracted paragraph.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-arm pilot study ANBL19P1 (NCT04385277) of post-consolidation chemoimmunotherapy for high-risk neuroblastoma. The primary objective was feasibility of five cycles of dinutuximab plus chemotherapy without progression within 30 weeks. Milligram doses are not printed in this report.

schema.label: Treatment
schema.text: Five 28-day cycles of temozolomide and irinotecan on days 1 to 5, dinutuximab on days 2 to 5, and sargramostim (GM-CSF) on days 6 to 12. Isotretinoin on days 8 to 21 was given during cycles 1 to 6.

NCT04385277.schema_source: Trial report, Desai et al., Cancer 2026 (PMID 41527287). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Younger than 31 years at enrollment, high-risk neuroblastoma by COG criteria: INRGSS stage M with MYCN amplification at any age, stage M at age 18 months or older, stage MS with MYCN amplification, or stage L2 with MYCN amplification.

Tandem autologous stem-cell transplantation was required. Progressive disease by the 2017 International Neuroblastoma Response Criteria at any time since the initial diagnosis made the patient ineligible.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Multicenter single-arm phase II trial (FLUORO, NCT04962126) of atezolizumab plus obinutuzumab, with PET-adapted ultra-low-dose involved-site radiotherapy, for treatment-naive follicular lymphoma. The primary endpoint is the complete-response rate by Lugano criteria.

schema.label: Treatment
schema.text: Six induction cycles of atezolizumab 1200 mg and obinutuzumab 1000 mg intravenously every 21 days. Obinutuzumab cycle 1 also includes days 8 and 15. PET/CT after cycle 2 determines radiotherapy: residual FDG-avid nodes larger than 1 cm receive 4 Gy in 2 fractions on two consecutive days to the involved sites, with a maximum of six involved-site fields. Patients in stable disease, partial response, or complete response after induction receive maintenance obinutuzumab 1000 mg every 8 weeks for up to 12 doses. Patients with progressive disease do not continue that maintenance path.

NCT04962126.schema_source: Trial report, Martynchyk et al., British Journal of Haematology 2026 (PMID 41949430). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Adults with treatment-naive grade 1 to 3A follicular lymphoma, Ann Arbor stage II to IV, ECOG 0 to 2, adequate organ function, measurable disease, and high tumor burden by at least one GELF or BNLI criterion.

Key exclusions include active autoimmune disease, immunosuppression, interstitial lung disease, and life-threatening complications that require urgent treatment. The remainder of the exclusion sentence is not fully printed in the extracted paragraph.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Investigator-initiated multicenter open-label randomized trial with blinded endpoint assessment (HALT AF, NCT05411614) comparing convergent hybrid ablation with catheter ablation for persistent atrial fibrillation and heart failure. About 120 participants are planned at five UK centers. This is not a radiotherapy trial.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Participants are randomized 1:1. Both arms aim to isolate the pulmonary veins and the posterior wall. Procedures are done under general anesthesia.

arms.label: Convergent hybrid ablation
arms.text: Epicardial posterior-pericardioscopic ablation, with or without left atrial appendage exclusion, followed by percutaneous endocardial ablation. The stages may occur in one admission or in two admissions, with the endocardial stage about 8 to 16 weeks after the epicardial stage when staged.

arms.label: Catheter ablation
arms.text: Endocardial catheter ablation alone, as a single-stage procedure, using radiofrequency or pulsed-field energy, until pulmonary-vein and posterior-wall isolation is achieved or judged impossible.

NCT05411614.schema_source: Study protocol, Ahmed et al., Journal of the American Heart Association 2026 (PMID 42216292). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Persistent atrial fibrillation with LVEF below 50%, covering mildly reduced and reduced ejection fraction. Rhythm control remains indicated after medical and lifestyle optimization, and there is clinical equipoise between hybrid ablation and catheter ablation.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Prospective multicenter single-arm study of watchful observation instead of prophylactic cranial irradiation after radical chemoradiotherapy for limited-stage small cell lung cancer.

schema.label: Treat
schema.text: No prophylactic cranial irradiation. Brain metastases that meet stereotactic criteria are treated with stereotactic radiotherapy. Other patients receive whole-brain radiotherapy.

arms.label: Observation, then focal or whole-brain radiotherapy if needed
arms.text: Stereotactic radiotherapy, specified at the 80% isodose: 20 Gy for lesions 20 mm or smaller and 18 Gy for 21 to 30 mm lesions. Eligibility for stereotactic treatment is 1 to 3 asymptomatic or minimally symptomatic lesions, each at most 30 mm, total volume under 15 ml, and the largest lesion under 10 ml. PTV is GTV plus 2 mm. Whole-brain radiotherapy, if used, is 30 Gy in 10 fractions of 2 Gy over 2 weeks.

NCT01166191.schema_source: Open-access protocol, Nawrocki et al., 2020 (PMID 32188425). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Limited-stage small cell lung cancer after radical chemoradiotherapy with remission or a good response, ECOG 0 to 2, and a brain MRI before chemoradiotherapy.
The printed eligibility table runs criteria together. Readable exclusions include no consent, disseminated disease, MRI contraindication, inability to do cognitive testing, and ECOG above 2.

followup.item: History, examination, brain MRI, and chest and abdomen CT
followup.window: The observation table lists visits through 24 to 36 months
followup.note: The published schedule grid is garbled, so individual month assignments are not restated. Neurocognitive tests and quality of life are listed on that table.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: JCOG1801A1 (CAP-LR) is a prospective observational ctDNA study of patients who meet the eligibility criteria of JCOG1801 and consent to the correlative study.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: In JCOG1801, patients are randomized 1:1. Adjuvant chemotherapy lasts 24 weeks and is CAPOX or modified FOLFOX6. Patients with poor performance status or neuropathy receive capecitabine or fluorouracil plus leucovorin.

arms.label: Up-front surgery
arms.text: Curative resection, then 24 weeks of adjuvant chemotherapy.

arms.label: Preoperative chemoradiotherapy
arms.text: Capecitabine 1650 mg/m2 per day for 28 days with radiotherapy 50.4 Gy in 28 fractions, then curative surgery and the same adjuvant chemotherapy.

NCT04288999.schema_source: Open-access correlative protocol, Hashimoto et al., BMJ Open 2023 (PMID 37586869). Read from the full text. The paper states the JCOG1801 treatment arms.

specimens.window: Sampling schedule is described for the correlative study
specimens.note: The printed schedule sentence is cut off after the treatment description, so individual draw times are not restated.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: PRaG 2.0E is a single-center single-arm phase II trial for refractory advanced NSCLC. Imaging is every 6 weeks by RECIST 1.1, irRECIST, and iRECIST. Adverse events use CTCAE v5.0 through 90 days after treatment.

schema.label: Treat
schema.text: Cycles are 21 days. At least two combination cycles, then PD-1 inhibitor plus Endostar until progression or intolerable toxicity.

arms.label: PRaG 2.0E
arms.text: Radiotherapy on day 1 to an unirradiated lesion, 10 to 24 Gy in 2 to 3 fractions of 5 to 8 Gy, once daily. Endostar 210 mg by continuous infusion over 72 hours from day 1. GM-CSF 200 micrograms subcutaneously daily for 7 days starting the day after radiotherapy. IL-2, 2 million IU subcutaneously daily for 7 days, starts the day after GM-CSF. The PD-1 inhibitor is given within one week after radiotherapy.

NCT06047860.schema_source: Open-access protocol, Huang et al., Translational Lung Cancer Research 2026 (PMID 42291342). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Age 18 to 75. Recurrent or metastatic NSCLC after platinum doublet chemotherapy and immune checkpoint inhibition, with no guideline standard option or intolerance, and at least one measurable metastasis over 1 cm.

No recent unstable cardiac disease. Troponin below the reference limit. LVEF over 55% without new wall-motion abnormality or severe structural disease. ECOG 0 to 3 and life expectancy at least 3 months.

Excluded: pregnancy or breastfeeding, another malignancy within 5 years except treated skin cancer or cervical carcinoma in situ, uncontrolled seizures or severe psychiatric disease, and active significant cardiac disease including LVEF under 50%.

followup.item: Survival contact
followup.window: Every 6 weeks after treatment until death, loss, withdrawal, or sponsor closure
followup.note: Adverse events are recorded up to 90 days after treatment.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: LANCE is an open-label single-center randomized noncomparative phase II selection trial of FLASH versus conventional electron radiotherapy for localized cutaneous squamous cell or basal cell carcinoma that is not suitable for surgery.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients are allocated to FLASH or conventional radiotherapy. Dose depends on lesion size. Inclusion and exclusion details are in Table 1.

arms.label: Small lesion, FLASH
arms.text: T1, 20 mm or smaller: 22 Gy in one fraction. 9 MeV electrons, 10 pulses of 2.2 Gy at 90 Hz, mean dose rate 220 Gy/s.

arms.label: Small lesion, conventional
arms.text: 22 Gy in one fraction at about 2 to 8 Gy/min with 10 MeV electrons and a 5 to 10 mm bolus.

arms.label: Large lesion, FLASH
arms.text: T2, over 20 mm to 40 mm: 30 Gy in 5 fractions of 6 Gy in less than 2 weeks. Each fraction is 3 pulses of 2 Gy, mean dose rate 270 Gy/s.

arms.label: Large lesion, conventional
arms.text: 30 Gy in 5 fractions of 6 Gy in less than 2 weeks at a conventional dose rate.

NCT07455331.schema_source: Open-access protocol, Kinj et al., 2024 (PMID 38362466). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Localized T1 or T2, N0 M0 cutaneous squamous cell or basal cell carcinoma. Surgery is declined or not possible, as judged by the tumor board.
The full inclusion and exclusion lists are in Table 1 and are not reprinted as prose.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: PredicT is a study of radiotherapy response, toxicity, and functional outcomes in extremity or limb-girdle soft tissue sarcoma. Radiotherapy is given according to local preoperative, postoperative, or palliative practice. Neoadjuvant chemotherapy is allowed. No trial-specific dose is printed.

NCT02520128.schema_source: Open-access protocol, Simoes et al., BMJ Open 2024 (PMID 39122389). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Histologic soft tissue sarcoma of the upper or lower limb or limb girdle. Age at least 16. WHO performance status 0 to 2. Fit for radiotherapy and willing to attend follow-up for 2 years.
Contraception for 3 months after treatment when relevant. Written consent.
Excluded: prior radiotherapy to the same site, pregnancy, or another malignancy that would compromise the endpoints.

followup.item: Follow-up visits
followup.window: During 2 years
followup.note: Patients must be willing to attend. A visit-by-visit calendar is not printed in the extracted eligibility text.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-arm phase II trial, 2017 to 2024, of intensified conditioning with total marrow irradiation for adults at high risk of relapse.

schema.label: Treat
schema.text: Total marrow irradiation 1.5 Gy twice daily on days -3 to -1, about 8 hours apart, total 9 Gy, with myeloablative chemotherapy. Plans use Eclipse.

arms.label: TMI conditioning
arms.text: 9 Gy total marrow irradiation in six fractions of 1.5 Gy.

NCT03121014.schema_source: Trial report, Maahs et al., Haematologica 2025 (PMID 40534485). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Age 18 to 65. AML, MDS, or CML at high risk of relapse. High-risk AML includes relapsed or refractory disease and poor-risk AML in first remission by European LeukemiaNet. MDS risk uses poor-risk cytogenetics.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: IMPORT LOW is a multicenter randomized phase 3 noninferiority trial after breast conservation.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Three radiotherapy schedules. Surgical clips were strongly recommended to localize the tumor bed.

arms.label: Whole breast
arms.text: 40 Gy in 15 fractions to the whole breast.

arms.label: Reduced dose
arms.text: 36 Gy in 15 fractions to the whole breast and 40 Gy in 15 fractions to the partial breast.

arms.label: Partial breast
arms.text: 40 Gy in 15 fractions to the partial breast only.

NCT00814567.schema_source: Trial report, Coles et al., 2017 (PMID 28779963). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Women age 50 or older after breast-conserving surgery for unifocal invasive ductal adenocarcinoma, not classical lobular carcinoma, any grade.
Pathologic tumor size 3 cm or less, pN0 or one to three positive nodes, and margins of at least 2 mm.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Multicenter unblinded randomized trial at 16 Canadian centers for medically inoperable stage I NSCLC. Accrual closed early. 233 patients were randomized, 154 to SBRT and 79 to conventional radiotherapy.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Tumor size (T1, 3 cm or smaller, versus T2a, over 3 to 5 cm), peripheral versus central location, and institution.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Randomization is 2:1.

arms.label: SBRT
arms.text: 48 Gy in 4 alternate-day fractions for peripheral tumors, or 60 Gy in 8 daily fractions for central tumors.

arms.label: Hypofractionated radiotherapy
arms.text: 60 Gy in 15 daily fractions.

NCT03924869.schema_source: Trial report, Swaminath et al., JAMA Oncology 2024 (PMID 39298144). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Medically inoperable T1 or T2a N0 M0 NSCLC, confirmed histologically or by a suspicious nodule with malignant FDG uptake.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Randomized open-label phase 3 noninferiority trial at 7 Chinese hospitals. Primary endpoint is progression-free survival. A radiotherapy or chemotherapy dose is not stated in the sentences read here.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Computer 1:1 randomization at Zhejiang Cancer Hospital. Open label.

arms.label: Radiotherapy
arms.text: Radiotherapy alone.

arms.label: Concurrent chemoradiotherapy
arms.text: Concurrent chemoradiotherapy.

NCT03015727.schema_source: Trial report, Jin et al., BMC Medicine 2026 (PMID 42436536). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Newly diagnosed nonkeratinizing nasopharyngeal carcinoma, T3 to T4 and/or N2 to N3 by AJCC 7th edition, no distant metastasis, Karnofsky performance status at least 70, and adequate liver, renal, and hematologic function.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Phase II trial of stereotactic ablative radiotherapy integrated with resection for early non-small cell lung cancer. This paper reports interim safety.

schema.label: Treat
schema.text: Risk-adapted SABR, delivered every other day.

arms.label: SABR
arms.text: 54 Gy in 3 fractions, 55 Gy in 5 fractions, or 60 Gy in 8 fractions, chosen by tumor size and location.

NCT02136355.schema_source: Trial report, Palma et al., Radiation Oncology 2017 (PMID 28129789). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Histologically confirmed T1 or T2a non-small cell lung cancer, 5 cm or smaller, node negative and without distant metastases.
Age 18 or older, consent, ECOG 0 to 2, and life expectancy over 6 months.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Allogeneic bone marrow transplantation for sickle cell disease using post-transplantation cyclophosphamide and low-dose total body irradiation. The paper says eligibility and treatment were reported previously and restates the conditioning used.

schema.label: Treat
schema.text: Nonmyeloablative conditioning and a single fraction of total body irradiation.

arms.label: Conditioning
arms.text: Rabbit antithymocyte globulin 0.5 mg/kg on day -9 and 2 mg/kg on days -8 and -7. Fludarabine 30 mg/m2 per day on days -6 to -2. Cyclophosphamide 14.5 mg/kg on days -6 and -5. Total body irradiation 400 cGy in one fraction on day -1.

NCT00489281.schema_source: Trial report, Goldenberg et al., Blood Advances 2026 (PMID 41569644). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Age 2 to 70 with at least one eligible related donor, haploidentical or matched. Sickle genotypes include Hb SS and the compound genotypes listed in the paper.
At least one severe complication warranting transplant, including stroke. The paper says the full eligibility was reported previously.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Prospective single-center open-label nonrandomized two-arm comparison of normofractionated and hypofractionated tangential IMRT after breast conservation. The sample-size calculation was for 226 patients. Fraction doses are not stated in the sentences read here.

NCT01403779.schema_source: Trial report, Sarria et al., 2022 (PMID 35600361). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Unilateral breast cancer, age 60 or older, stage pTis to pT3, pN0 to pN1a, M0 by TNM 7th edition, after breast-conserving surgery, any molecular profile.

followup.item: Late skin and soft-tissue effects
followup.window: About 2 years
followup.note: The expected rate and the later amendment about telangiectasia grade refer to assessment after 2 years.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Comparison of short-course and long-course preoperative chemoradiotherapy for rectal adenocarcinoma, using patients from KROG 10-01, KROG 11-02 (NCT01431599), and the long-course cohort.

schema.label: Treat
schema.text: KROG 11-02 used 33 Gy in 10 fractions with capecitabine. The same paper states the other schedules used in the comparison.

arms.label: KROG 11-02
arms.text: 33 Gy in 10 fractions with capecitabine 825 mg/m2 twice daily.

arms.label: KROG 10-01
arms.text: 25 Gy in 5 fractions with fluorouracil 400 mg/m2 per day.

arms.label: Long course
arms.text: 45 Gy in 25 fractions plus a 5.4 Gy boost in 3 fractions to the rectal mass.

NCT01431599.schema_source: Trial report, Lee et al., Cancer Research and Treatment 2017 (PMID 29161802). Read from the full text. The paper also reports the companion KROG schedules.
eligibility: Histologically confirmed rectal adenocarcinoma, cT3 to T4 and N0 to N2 on MRI and/or endorectal ultrasound, no distant metastasis, no other malignancy except nonmelanoma skin cancer, ECOG 0 to 2, and adequate marrow, liver, and renal function.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: EORTC 1560 (ILOC) is a single-arm multicenter early phase II study of partial local ablation plus durvalumab and tremelimumab for microsatellite-stable metastatic colorectal cancer with unresectable colorectal liver metastases after disease stabilization on chemotherapy. Drug doses are not stated in the sentences read here.

schema.label: Treat
schema.text: Partial radiofrequency ablation or stereotactic radiotherapy of a liver metastasis, with dual checkpoint blockade.

arms.label: Partial ablation plus durvalumab and tremelimumab
arms.text: Local partial ablation concurrent with durvalumab and tremelimumab.

NCT03101475.schema_source: Trial report, Seligmann et al., 2025 (PMID 40706222). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Histologically confirmed colorectal cancer with liver metastases. Extrahepatic disease, if present, is limited to two sites, each lesion 5 cm or smaller, and not curable by resection, ablation, or radiotherapy.
Age over 18. Further criteria are started in the methods and are not fully printed in the extracted sentence.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Multicenter open-label randomized phase 2 trial of radiochemotherapy with or without cetuximab for unresectable esophageal cancer, 2011 to 2016.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: 3D radiotherapy. Planned dose 50.4 Gy in 28 fractions to the primary tumor and locoregional nodes. After 4 to 4.5 weeks, resectable patients who accept surgery stop at 45 Gy. Chemotherapy drugs are not named in the sentences read here.

arms.label: Radiochemotherapy plus cetuximab
arms.text: Radiochemotherapy with cetuximab.

arms.label: Radiochemotherapy
arms.text: Radiochemotherapy without cetuximab.

NCT01787006.schema_source: Trial report, Rades et al., Strahlentherapie und Onkologie 2020 (PMID 32533228). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Histologically confirmed unresectable esophageal cancer.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: ACOSOG Z11102 is a prospective single-arm noninferiority trial of breast conservation for two or three malignant sites in one breast. This report is the initial feasibility analysis. A radiotherapy dose is not stated in the sentences read here.

NCT01556243.schema_source: Trial report, Rosenkranz et al., Annals of Surgical Oncology 2018 (PMID 29987605). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Women with two or three sites of malignancy in a single breast. Inclusion criteria are introduced in the methods and are not fully printed in the extracted sentence. 198 of 223 eligible patients were enrolled before surgery and are the subject of this report.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: MISTIC is a European unblinded randomized trial in men receiving radiotherapy for prostate cancer. The instillation schedule is not stated in the sentences read here.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Centre-specific 1:1 lists from Random Allocation Software. Treatment is not masked.

arms.label: iAluRil
arms.text: Intravesical sodium hyaluronate and chondroitin sulfate (iAluRil) added to radiotherapy.

arms.label: No additional treatment
arms.text: Radiotherapy without iAluRil.

NCT03493997.schema_source: Trial report, Redorta et al., 2021 (PMID 34337507). Read from the full text.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: MASPAC is a prospective two-arm randomized international trial of MR-guided adaptive SBRT to the primary pancreatic tumor for pain control in metastatic pancreatic cancer. Also registered as DRKS 00025801. An SBRT dose is not stated in the sentences read here.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Registration is stratified by age and ECOG performance status.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients are registered after consent. SBRT is studied after 8 weeks of standard palliative chemotherapy.

arms.label: MR-guided SBRT
arms.text: MR-guided adaptive SBRT to the primary tumor plus continued standard care.

arms.label: Standard care
arms.text: Standard palliative care without primary-tumor SBRT.

NCT05114213.schema_source: Open-access protocol, Pavic et al., Radiation Oncology 2022 (PMID 35078490). Read from the full text.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: MC1635 is a randomized phase III trial of whole-breast radiotherapy. The primary objective is the complication rate. Total dose in gray is not stated in the sentences read here.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: The regimens are compared with or without a boost, and with photons or protons.

arms.label: 5 fractions
arms.text: Ultra-hypofractionated whole-breast radiotherapy in 5 fractions.

arms.label: 15 fractions
arms.text: Hypofractionated whole-breast radiotherapy in 15 fractions.

NCT03324802.schema_source: Trial report, Vargas et al., 2025 (PMID 40842574). Read from the full text.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-arm multicenter phase II trial (NOAHS-ARC) in Santiago, Chile. Primary endpoint is complete tumor response, combining pathologic complete response and sustained clinical complete response beyond 1 year, compared with a historical 12% rate. Target accrual is 48 evaluable patients. Interim look at 24 patients.

schema.label: Treatment
schema.text: Induction short-course radiotherapy, 25 Gy in five fractions of 5 Gy. Seven to 14 days later, consolidation chemotherapy with either nine cycles of FOLFOX every 14 days (oxaliplatin 85 mg/m2, leucovorin 400 mg/m2, 5-fluorouracil bolus 400 mg/m2, and 5-fluorouracil infusion 2400 mg/m2 over 46 hours) or six cycles of CAPOX every 21 days (capecitabine 1000 mg/m2 every 12 hours for 14 days and oxaliplatin 130 mg/m2 on day 1). Response is assessed 4 to 8 weeks after chemotherapy. Clinical complete response may be managed without surgery. Near-complete response is reassessed at 4 weeks. Incomplete response goes to total mesorectal excision.

NCT04864067.schema_source: Open-access protocol, Quezada-Diaz et al., International Journal of Colorectal Disease 2025 (PMID 40100473). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Biopsy-proven mismatch-repair-proficient rectal adenocarcinoma, MRI stage II (T3 to 4, N0) or III (any T, N1 or higher), less than 7 cm from the anal verge and palpable. Age over 18. No prior rectal cancer.

Excluded: stage IV, mismatch-repair deficiency, tumor beyond 7 cm or not palpable, exenteration, ECOG above 1, recurrent disease, contraindication to radiotherapy, chemotherapy, or MRI, untreated coronary disease, acute coronary syndrome within 12 months, heart failure, neuropathy, pregnancy or breastfeeding.

Baseline laboratories used for exclusion: hemoglobin under 8 g/dL, white cells under 4000/L as printed, platelets under 100,000/L, creatinine clearance under 50 mL/min. The narrative excludes total bilirubin above 5 mg/dL, while the eligibility table prints the inequality in the opposite direction.

pretreatment.item: Digital exam, flexible sigmoidoscopy with biopsy, rectal MRI, CT chest/abdomen/pelvis, and bloodwork
pretreatment.note: Repeated at mid-chemotherapy (9 weeks after chemotherapy starts) and 4 weeks after chemotherapy ends.

during.item: Blood count, renal panel, and hepatic panel
during.note: Toxicity graded with CTCAE version 5.0.

during.item: Surgeon re-evaluation with exam, sigmoidoscopy and biopsy, rectal MRI, and bloodwork
during.window: Mid total neoadjuvant therapy and at completion
during.note: Mid-treatment response does not stop chemotherapy.

followup.item: After total mesorectal excision
followup.window: At least 2 years
followup.note: Exam every 4 months, CEA and blood count every 4 months, CT chest/abdomen/pelvis at 12 and 24 months, and colonoscopy at 12 and 24 months.

followup.item: Watch and wait
followup.window: At least 2 years
followup.note: Exam with digital exam and flexible sigmoidoscopy every 4 months, CBC and CEA every 4 months, annual CT, rectal MRI every 6 months, and annual colonoscopy. Local regrowth leads to a recommendation for excision.

specimens.window: Longitudinally during treatment
specimens.note: Biopsies are fixed and paraffin embedded. An extra 3 mL EDTA blood sample is centrifuged and plasma stored at -80 C for later circulating-tumor DNA analysis.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-arm phase II trial for veterans with de novo oligometastatic prostate cancer. Primary endpoint is the percent of patients with PSA under 0.05 ng/mL six months after testosterone recovers to at least 150 ng/dL. Evaluable sample size is 25, total 28 allowing for testosterone non-recovery. Protocol version 3, 26 March 2018.

schema.label: Treatment
schema.text: Radical prostatectomy with pelvic node dissection first. If pT3a or higher, positive margins, or N1, postoperative IMRT to pelvic nodes 45 to 50.4 Gy and prostate bed 66 to 72 Gy in conventional fractionation. Within 0 to 3 days after surgery: one 45 mg subcutaneous leuprolide depot, apalutamide 240 mg orally daily, and abiraterone 1000 mg orally daily with prednisone 10 mg daily, for six months. SBRT to all visible M1a/b sites within two months of starting androgen deprivation. Recommended SBRT is 6 to 8 Gy x 5, 9 to 12 Gy x 3, or 16 to 18 Gy x 1. A BED above 100 Gy (alpha/beta 3) is a goal but not required.

NCT03298087.schema_source: Open-access protocol, Parikh et al., BMC Cancer 2019 (PMID 30935383). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Biopsy-proven prostate adenocarcinoma, age at least 18, M1a/b with 1 to 5 visible metastases on NaF PET/CT or PSMA PET/CT plus CT chest/abdomen/pelvis. Pelvic nodes of any number are allowed if the largest is under 2 cm. No visceral metastases. ECOG 0 or 1. Testosterone above 200 ng/dL before androgen deprivation. Fit for prostatectomy, metastasis SBRT, and androgen deprivation.

Hemoglobin at least 9.0 g/dL and platelets at least 100,000 x 10^9/microliter as printed, both independent of transfusion or growth factors within 3 months. Albumin at least 3.0 g/dL, GFR at least 45 mL/min, potassium at least 3.5 mmol/L, bilirubin at most 1.5 times the upper limit, AST or ALT under 2.5 times the upper limit. The printed platelet unit is not restated as a corrected value.

Biopsy of one metastasis should be attempted unless unsafe. If not diagnostic, a second imaging modality must agree. Excluded: small-cell histology, spinal cord compression, prior pelvic malignancy or pelvic radiation, inflammatory bowel disease, seizure history, and specified cardiovascular events within 6 months.

pretreatment.item: NaF or PSMA PET/CT with CT of chest, abdomen, and pelvis
pretreatment.note: PSA and total testosterone are also drawn at inclusion.

during.item: PSA, testosterone, quality of life, and toxicity
during.note: Pill counts monthly during the six months of apalutamide and abiraterone. SBRT is given between day 30 and day 60. Systemic therapy stops at 6 months. CTCAE version 4.

followup.item: Visits
followup.window: Every 30 days for the first year, then every 3 months
followup.note: Patients remain on study until unacceptable toxicity, progression, withdrawal, or two years. PSA and testosterone continue every 3 months after the first year on the visit table.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Nonrandomized phase II trial (PART) of elective para-aortic radiotherapy for pN1 prostate cancer. Primary endpoint is 5-year clinical relapse-free survival.

schema.label: Treatment
schema.text: Pelvic and para-aortic node PTV D98 is 45 Gy in 25 fractions of 1.8 Gy. After prostatectomy, the prostate and seminal-vesicle bed median dose is 70 Gy in 35 fractions. For primary prostate radiotherapy, the median PTV dose is 65 Gy in 25 fractions. Daily cone-beam CT is required. Androgen deprivation starts 2 to 4 weeks before radiotherapy and continues for 24 months. Either an LHRH analogue or an antagonist is allowed.

NCT03079323.schema_source: Open-access protocol, Draulans et al., JMIR Research Protocols 2018 (PMID 30545809). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Men older than 18 with biopsy-proven prostate adenocarcinoma, cT1 to 4, referred for primary high-dose radiotherapy, or after prostatectomy (pT2 to 4), with pN1 disease after extended pelvic node dissection.
pN1 must meet one of: two or more positive nodes, positive nodes comprising more than 7% of nodes removed, or extracapsular extension of any nodal metastasis.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Prospective single-arm phase II study (ePRO-PICCRT) of locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma. Primary endpoint is pathologic complete response. Assignment after the first cycle depends on patient-reported dysphagia relief, not randomization.

schema.label: Treatment
schema.text: Cycle 1 for all patients: albumin-bound paclitaxel 260 mg/m2 on day 1, carboplatin AUC 5 or cisplatin 60 mg/m2 on day 1, and tislelizumab 200 mg on day 1. Early remission is more than 70% relief on the EORTC OES-18 dysphagia score. That group continues the same regimen for two further cycles. The latent-remission group receives one further cycle, then short-course radiotherapy 30 Gy in 10 daily fractions of 3 Gy (days 1 to 5 and 16 to 20) with tislelizumab 200 mg on day 2, albumin-bound paclitaxel 60 mg/m2 on days 1, 8, and 15, and carboplatin AUC 2 on days 1, 8, and 15 or cisplatin 60 mg/m2 on day 1. Radical esophagectomy with lymphadenectomy is planned 4 to 6 weeks later. Voluntary immunotherapy every 3 weeks for up to 1 year may follow surgery.

NCT05596890.schema_source: Open-access protocol, Huang et al., Journal of Thoracic Disease 2024 (PMID 39144362). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Pathologically confirmed, treatment-naive, potentially resectable esophageal squamous cell carcinoma: cT1 to 4a N1 to 2 M0 or cT3 to 4a N0 M0. Age 18 to 75. Expected survival over 6 months. ECOG 0 to 2. Adequate organ function, without numeric cutoffs in the criteria list.

Excluded: prior thoracic surgery or radiation, cervical or multi-origin esophageal cancer, fistula, peripheral neuropathy, another cancer, autoimmune or immunodeficiency disease, diabetes longer than 10 years or poor control, interstitial lung disease, active hepatitis B or C, and pregnancy or lactation.

pretreatment.item: History, examination, weight, ECOG, routine tests, quality of life, and Nutritional Risk Screening 2002

followup.item: Clinic visits
followup.window: Every 3 months for 2 years after surgery, every 6 months in years 3 to 5, then annually
followup.note: EORTC OES-18 and QLQ-C30 are collected through the end of each cycle before surgery and every 3 months after surgery. Grade 3 or 4 adverse events use CTCAE version 5.0.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-arm, nonrandomized phase II trial in metastatic microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer (n=40) and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (n=25). ECOG 0 or 1. Primary endpoint is disease control rate by intention to treat.

schema.label: Treatment
schema.text: Radiation, ipilimumab, and nivolumab. Radiotherapy is 24 Gy in three fractions of 8 Gy, given every other day, to a lesion that can meet dose constraints. A second unirradiated lesion is required for assessment.
